title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
今年乙卯順天府鄉試廼我
皇上龍飛之第十二科也考試官
諭德臣維楨侍講臣煒皆以
上命至同考試官進士臣復臣溱
知縣臣孔墀教諭臣應和臣
樞臣梅臣棟臣大魁臣成式
===
皆以聘至監試官御史臣冀
臣俊皆以
請至其諸執事人衆則皆府尹臣
燿府丞臣鏜辟至而臣鏜則
職在提調董一切簾内外事
先至諸臣咸至矣既分之而
各執乃事矣臣乃進提學御

順天府鄉試錄序

今年乙卯，順天府鄉試廼我皇上龍飛之第十二科也。考試官諭德臣維楨、侍講臣煒，皆以上命至。同考試官進士臣復、臣溱，知縣臣孔墀，教諭臣應和、臣樞、臣梅、臣棟、臣大魁、臣成式，皆以聘至。監試官御史臣冀、臣俊，皆以請至。其諸執事人衆，則皆府尹臣燿、府丞臣鏜辟至。而臣鏜則職在提調，董一切簾内外事，先至。諸臣咸至矣，既分之而各執乃事矣，臣乃進提學御
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

This year, yimao [1555], the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination is the twelfth examination held since our Emperor ascended the throne. The Examiners, your servants Weizhen, Admonisher, and Wei, Expositor, both arrived by imperial command. The Associate Examiners—your servants Fu and Zhen, metropolitan graduates (jinshi); Kongchi, District Magistrate; and Yinghe, Shu, Mei, Dong, Dakui, and Chengshi, Instructors— all came by invitation. The officials overseeing the examination, your servants Ji and Jun, both Investigating Censors, came upon request. The numerous other functionaries were all engaged by your servants Yao, Prefect, and Tang, Vice-Prefect.

As for your servant Tang, my duties were those of Proctor, directing all affairs both inside and outside the examination curtain, and I arrived first. Once all the officials had arrived, duties were apportioned and each took up his assigned work. I then presented [the candidates selected by] the censor supervising education …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
史臣馬三才所選士及諸曹
六舘所選士三試焉乃復加
志掄選錄雋者一百三十有
五人焉士既錄簾內外諸臣
始相見乃喜而相慶曰嗟乎
良哉選也藉是可以報
天子矣然臣維楨顧有懼焉今者
===
臣手錄以
獻之
上也色勃勃而不能持足盤盤而
不能前誠懼之也臣聞之往
古士有才賢而不獲進有司
罪無赦進矣而才賢者不果
効有司之罪亦無赦何者不

punctuated:
史臣馬三才所選士及諸曹、六舘所選士，三試焉，乃復加志掄選，錄雋者一百三十有五人焉。士既錄，簾內外諸臣始相見，乃喜而相慶曰：「嗟乎，良哉選也！藉是可以報天子矣。」
然臣維楨顧有懼焉。今者臣手錄以獻之上也，色勃勃而不能持，足盤盤而不能前，誠懼之也。臣聞之往古：士有才賢而不獲進，有司罪無赦；進矣而才賢者不果効，有司之罪亦無赦。何者？不
translation_en:
…the candidates selected by your servant Ma Sancai, the censor supervising education, together with those selected by the various offices and the Six Colleges, and examined them in three sessions. We then devoted further attention [?] to selection, recording the names of 135 outstanding candidates. Once the candidates had been selected, the officials serving inside and outside the examination enclosure met one another for the first time. Delighted, they congratulated one another, saying: “Ah, what an excellent selection! Through this we can repay the Son of Heaven.”
Yet I, your servant Weizhen, have misgivings. Now, as I personally prepare this record to present to Your Majesty, my expression betrays an agitation I cannot control, and my feet hesitate, unable to advance. Truly, I am afraid. I have heard this teaching from antiquity: when talented and worthy scholars fail to obtain advancement, the responsible officials bear an unpardonable fault; when they have been advanced but fail to prove their talent and worth in service, the responsible officials likewise bear an unpardonable fault. Why is this? Because they are not…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
智之故也今夫所貴乎樹木
者樹松栢也其次樹桃李松
栢可材桃李華悅人所不足
不任風雨然不與荆棘倫矣
即若不意松栢化而為桃李
桃李又化而為荆棘持是以
譙呵樹者則樹者口噤莫為
===
應彼其初固嘗植之也夫樹
人亦類乎是者臣恐其或類
之也故懼臣關中人也頃者
臣自關中来而渡于孟津見
有轉大木于河滸者前呼輿
諤後皆應之木翩然如馳焉
當是時也即有齊謳郢調吳
alt_text:
智之故也今夫所貴乎樹木
者樹松栢也其次樹桃李松
栢可材桃李華悅人所不足
不任風雨然不與荊棘倫矣
即若不意松栢化而爲桃李
桃李又化而爲荊棘持是以
譙呵樹者則樹者口噤莫爲
===
應彼其初固嘗植之也夫樹
人亦類乎是者臣恐其或類
之也故懼臣關中人也頃者
臣自關中來而渡于孟津見
有轉大木于河滸者前呼輿
謣後皆應之木翩然如駛焉
當是時也即有齊謳郢調吳
punctuated:
智之故也。今夫所貴乎樹木者，樹松栢也；其次樹桃李。松栢可材，桃李華悅人，所不足，不任風雨，然不與荆棘倫矣。即若不意松栢化而為桃李，桃李又化而為荆棘，持是以譙呵樹者，則樹者口噤莫為應，彼其初固嘗植之也。夫樹人亦類乎是者，臣恐其或類之也，故懼。
臣關中人也。頃者，臣自關中来而渡于孟津，見有轉大木于河滸者，前呼輿諤，後皆應之，木翩然如馳焉。當是時也，即有齊謳、郢調、吳
translation_en:
…because of a lack of discernment. Now, in planting trees, what is most valued is planting pines and cypresses; next come peaches and plums. Pines and cypresses furnish timber, while peach and plum blossoms delight people. The latter’s shortcoming is that they cannot withstand wind and rain, yet they are certainly not to be ranked with brambles and thorns. Suppose, however, that pines and cypresses unexpectedly turned into peaches and plums, and peaches and plums in turn became brambles and thorns. If this were grounds for rebuking the planter, he would be left speechless, unable to reply: he had, after all, planted them in the first place. Cultivating men is much like this. Your servant fears that something similar might happen, and therefore feels apprehensive.
Your servant is a man of Guanzhong. Recently, coming from Guanzhong and crossing the river at Mengjin, I saw men moving a great log along the riverbank. Those in front shouted a cry [?], and those behind all answered; the log moved lightly and swiftly, as though racing along. At that moment, even had there been songs of Qi, melodies of Ying, and Wu…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
歆越吟與夫激羽流商之奏
截雲下塵之曲悉末之用矣
臣以此則嘆以爲侈言無當
而繁華沒實故今校諸生之
文則直掇大指而棄其雕蟲
蓋竊有悟于轉大木之事也
既行而入燕趙之間則今
畿内地也在昔燕趙之間猶多
竒偉俶儻之士今其人已往
其聲猶存也臣乃頓步躊躇
于境上者乆之即其人雖不
純于先王之道然以効節不
顧身盡公而不徇私固亦有
足多者焉今此諸生以誦說
alt_text:
歈越吟與夫激羽流商之奏
截雲下塵之曲悉末之用矣
臣以此則嘆以爲侈言無當
而繁華沒實故今校諸生之
文則直掇大指而棄其雕蟲
蓋竊有悟于轉大木之事也
既行而又燕趙之間則今
===
畿内地也在昔燕趙之間猶多
奇偉俶儻之士今其人已往
其聲猶存也臣乃頻步躊躇
于境上者久之即其人雖不
純于先王之道然以効節不
顧身盡公而不徇私固亦有
足多者焉今此諸生以誦説
punctuated:
歆、越吟，與夫激羽流商之奏、截雲下塵之曲，悉末之用矣。臣以此則嘆，以爲侈言無當，而繁華沒實。故今校諸生之文，則直掇大指，而棄其雕蟲，蓋竊有悟于轉大木之事也。
既行而入燕趙之間，則今畿内地也。在昔燕趙之間，猶多竒偉俶儻之士。今其人已往，其聲猶存也。臣乃頓步躊躇于境上者乆之。即其人雖不純于先王之道，然以効節不顧身，盡公而不徇私，固亦有足多者焉。今此諸生以誦說
translation_en:
…songs [?] and chants of Yue, together with performances that stir the yu and flow through the shang musical tones, and melodies that halt the clouds and shake down the dust—all were of no use [?]. This prompted your servant to sigh, reflecting that extravagant words serve no purpose and florid ornament obscures substance. Thus, in assessing the candidates’ compositions now, I take only their main purport and discard their petty verbal embellishments. In this, I have privately gained some insight from the business of moving the great timber.
Continuing my journey, I entered the region of Yan and Zhao, now the territory surrounding the capital. In former times, Yan and Zhao abounded in men of extraordinary stature and unrestrained spirit. Though those men are now gone, their renown endures. Your servant therefore halted at the region’s border and lingered in reflection for a long time. Although these men did not adhere wholly to the Way of the former kings, their devoted service without regard for their own lives, and their wholehearted commitment to public duty without yielding to private interests, surely deserve considerable praise. Now these candidates, through recitation and exposition…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
詩書稱引先王則人人能矣
今之受事而竒偉俶儻之氣
如彼何故臣猶願諸生之慕
之也今
國家建都于燕四方奉贄納貢
之臣繈屬而至其諸齒角羽
毛百物珍異皆
===
===
御府所餘常山在其右遼海在
其左厥形險固造物者故設
此以作藩垣又
國家所有然所貴者唯獨節士
之幹與忠義之腹耳異日者
諸生誠養有節士之幹而懷
忠義之腹則臣且望下風而

之幹與忠義之腹耳異〔日〕者
諸生誠養有節士之幹而懷
忠義之腹則〔臣〕且望下風而
punctuated:
詩書，稱引先王，則人人能矣。今之受事，而竒偉俶儻之氣如彼，何故？臣猶願諸生之慕之也。
今國家建都于燕，四方奉贄納貢之臣繈屬而至，其諸齒角羽毛、百物珍異，皆御府所餘。常山在其右，遼海在其左，厥形險固，造物者故設此以作藩垣，又國家所有。然所貴者，唯獨節士之幹與忠義之腹耳。異日者，諸生誠養有節士之幹，而懷忠義之腹，則臣且望下風而
translation_en:
…the Book of Poetry and the Book of Documents, and invoking the former kings—everyone can do this. Why do those undertaking service today possess such an extraordinary and untrammeled spirit as theirs [?]? Your servant would still wish these students to emulate them.
Now the dynasty has established its capital at Yan. Ministers from every quarter bearing presentation gifts and tribute arrive in an unbroken succession. Tusks, horns, feathers, pelts, and all manner of rare and precious objects abound in the imperial treasury. Changshan lies to its right and the Liaohai region to its left. Its terrain is naturally defensible and secure: the Creator deliberately placed these here to serve as protective walls, and these too belong to the dynasty. Yet what alone deserves to be prized is the steadfast mettle of men of integrity and a heart filled with loyalty and righteousness. If, in days to come, these students truly cultivate such mettle and harbor such hearts, then your servant will stand downwind of them in deference and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
拜之非拜諸生也拜節士與
忠義之夫也臣列在交戟之
內最乆竊覩
陛下之神明
天授之也即如一日之間
國家之大議凡幾其大事凡幾
然事皆炳于
===
前知而議皆成于
立斷諸司
奏疏而得報者咸抱疏吐舌以
爲弗及今此諸生竪儒耳豈
能奉奔走哉然臣私以爲世
無粹白之狐而有粹白之裘
所求者博所取者微也若是

===

立斷諸司
奏疏而得報者咸抱疏吐舌以
爲弗及今此諸生豎儒耳豈
能奉奔走哉然〔臣〕私以爲世
無粹白之狐而有粹白之裘
所求者博所取者微也若是
punctuated: 拜之，非拜諸生也，拜節士與忠義之夫也。臣列在交戟之內最乆，竊覩陛下之神明，天授之也。即如一日之間，國家之大議凡幾，其大事凡幾？然事皆炳于前知，而議皆成于立斷。諸司奏疏而得報者，咸抱疏吐舌，以爲弗及。今此諸生，竪儒耳，豈能奉奔走哉？然臣私以爲，世無粹白之狐，而有粹白之裘，所求者博，所取者微也。若是
translation_en: …bow to them. It is not to these students that I bow, but to men of integrity, loyalty, and righteousness. Your servant has served within the crossed halberds of the palace gates for a very long time, and has humbly observed that Your Majesty’s sagely discernment is Heaven-bestowed. Consider how many weighty deliberations and great affairs of state arise in a single day! Yet every affair is illuminated by Your Majesty’s foreknowledge, and every deliberation is settled by an immediate decision. Those in the various offices who submit memorials and receive replies all clutch their memorials and stick out their tongues in astonishment, acknowledging that they cannot match such powers. These students now are mere immature scholars: how could they carry out Your Majesty’s commands? Yet your servant privately believes that, although the world has no fox of pure white, it does have robes of pure-white fox fur: one seeks widely, taking only a little from each. If this is so…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
則臣乃敢以諸生
進矣而卒慮乎奔走之或後也
故事士既錄順天府有宴宴
諸生諸執事皆在焉臣將挾
持前說須詣宴所一一爲諸
生道之且因以爲勸焉而先
以謁諸同事諸同事曰夫勸
===
也若是而止歟於是臣應之
曰諸執事亦甞聞里父之醮
子乎里父之醮其子于客位
也爲之具三加著誡詞備矣
客曰且更有加乎里父曰無
以加也曩吾父所以醮吾者
固若是止矣今吾所以勸諸

客曰且更有加乎里父曰無
以加也曩吾父所以醮吾者
固若是止矣今吾所以勸諸
punctuated:
則臣乃敢以諸生進矣，而卒慮乎奔走之或後也。
故事，士既錄，順天府有宴，宴諸生，諸執事皆在焉。臣將挾持前說，須詣宴所，一一爲諸生道之，且因以爲勸焉，而先以謁諸同事。諸同事曰：「夫勸也，若是而止歟？」於是臣應之曰：「諸執事亦甞聞里父之醮子乎？里父之醮其子于客位也，爲之具三加，著誡詞，備矣。客曰：『且更有加乎？』里父曰：『無以加也。曩吾父所以醮吾者，固若是止矣。』今吾所以勸諸
translation_en:
… then your servant dares to present these students, yet still worries that they may fall behind in hastening to serve.
By established practice, once the successful candidates have been selected, Shuntian Prefecture holds a banquet for them, at which all the officials involved are present. Your servant intends to take the foregoing remarks to the banquet and explain them point by point to the students, using the occasion to encourage them. First, however, I presented these remarks to my colleagues. They said, “Is this all the encouragement you will offer?” I replied, “Have you gentlemen ever heard of the village father who offered his son the ceremonial wine at his capping? When he offered his son the wine at the guest’s place, he provided for the three successive cappings and set down the words of admonition. Everything was complete. A guest asked, ‘Is there anything further to add?’ The father said, ‘There is nothing to add. This was all my own father did when he offered me the ceremonial wine.’ Now, the exhortations I offer to these …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
生者固吾昔所受于先達先
生者也錄將
獻臣宜有序引其端乃謹具其
始末如此云
奉訓大夫右春坊右諭德王
維楨謹序

生者，固吾昔所受于先達先生者也。」錄將獻，臣宜有序，引其端，乃謹具其始末如此云。
奉訓大夫、右春坊右諭德王維楨謹序。
translation_en:
…to the students is precisely what I formerly received from the eminent teachers who preceded me.” As this record is about to be presented to the throne, I, your servant, ought to provide a preface introducing it. I have therefore respectfully set forth the circumstances from beginning to end as above.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Weizhen, Grand Master for Rendering Instruction and Right Admonisher in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

Proctors

===

必得其名必得其壽
以德服人者中心悅而誠服也如七十子
之服孔子也詩云自西自東自南自北
無思不服此之謂也

punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

仁以為已任，不亦重乎？

必得其名，必得其壽。

以德服人者，中心悅而誠服也，如七十子之服孔子也。《詩》云：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」此之謂也。

易

上下交而其志同也。

天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。

天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。

書

予欲觀古人之象：日月星辰、山、龍、華蟲，作會；宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻，絺繡，以五采彰
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Taking benevolence as one’s own responsibility—is this not a heavy burden?

He will surely attain renown; he will surely attain longevity.

When one wins people’s submission through virtue, they are pleased in their innermost hearts and submit sincerely, as the seventy disciples submitted to Kongzi. The Book of Odes says: “From the west and from the east, from the south and from the north, none thought of withholding submission.” This is what it means.

Book of Changes

Those above and those below interact, and their purposes are the same.

Heaven and earth move each other, and the myriad things are transformed and born. The sage moves people’s hearts, and all under Heaven is peaceful and harmonious. By observing what they move, one can discern the true dispositions of heaven, earth, and the myriad things.

Thus, what the gentleman dwells in and finds repose in is the sequence of the Changes; what he delights in and ponders is the wording of the lines.

The great virtue of heaven and earth is called generation; the great treasure of the sage is called sovereign position.

Book of Documents

I wish to see the emblematic designs of the ancients: the sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and pheasants, rendered in painting; ancestral sacrificial vessels, waterweed, fire, grains of rice, axe patterns, and paired bow-shaped patterns, worked in fine embroidery, using the five colors to make them manifest…

施于五色，作服，汝明。
聲教訖于四海。
一曰壽，二曰富，三曰康寧。
亦越文王、武王，克知三有宅心，灼見三有俊心，以敬事上帝，立民長伯。

詩
何彼穠矣，唐棣之華！曷不肅雝，王姬之車？
今適南畝，或耘或耔。黍稷薿薿，攸介攸止，烝我髦士。
以我齊明，與我犧羊，以社以方。我田既臧，農夫之慶。
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。
我受命溥將，自天降康，豐年穰穰。

春秋
夏，城中丘。〔隱公七年〕城祝丘。〔桓公五年〕冬，城向。〔桓公十六年〕冬，仲孫何忌會晉韓不信、齊高張、宋仲幾、衛世叔申、鄭國參、曹人、莒人、薛人、杞人、小邾人，城成周。〔昭〕
translation_en:
…displayed in the five colors to make ceremonial robes; you must make these distinctions clear.
Their civilizing instruction reached throughout the Four Seas.
The first is longevity; the second, wealth; the third, health and peace.
Furthermore, Kings Wen and Wu could understand the hearts of those occupying the three offices and clearly discern the hearts of the outstanding men suited to those offices. Thus they reverently served the Lord on High and established leaders and chiefs for the people.

Book of Odes
How luxuriant they are—the blossoms of the cherry tree! How could one fail to be reverent and harmonious before the carriage of the king’s daughter?
Now we go to the southern fields, some weeding, others banking earth around the roots. The millets grow luxuriantly. There the eminent take their places, and our distinguished men are assembled.
With our pure, bright grain offerings and our sacrificial sheep, we sacrifice to the god of the soil and the spirits of the four quarters. Our fields have yielded well: this is the farmers’ blessing.
The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather here and alight. In great abundance the king has worthy men, whom the ruler employs and who are dear to the Son of Heaven.
The mandate we received is vast and great. From Heaven comes well-being, with bountiful harvests in years of plenty.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, Zhongqiu was fortified. 〔Seventh year of Duke Yin.〕 Zhuqiu was fortified. 〔Fifth year of Duke Huan.〕 In winter, Xiang was fortified. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Huan.〕 In winter, Zhongsun Heji met with Han Buxin of Jin, Gao Zhang of Qi, Zhong Ji of Song, Shishu Shen of Wei, Guo Can of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Xue, Qi, and Xiao Zhu to fortify Chengzhou. 〔Duke Zhao …〕

春齊人陳人曹人伐宋莊公十四年
吳子使札来聘襄公二十九年
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公自至夾谷定公十
年

五國以為屬屬有長十國以為連連有帥

義近於禮
德也者得於身也故曰古之學術道者將
以得身也是故聖人務焉

公三十二年。
春，齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋。莊公十四年。
吳子使札来聘。襄公二十九年。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公自至夾谷。定公十年。

五國以為屬，屬有長；十國以為連，連有帥；三十國以為卒，卒有正；二百一十國以為州，州有伯。
仁者，義之本也，順之體也，得之者尊。
春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。
德也者，得於身也。故曰：古之學術道者，將以得身也。是故聖人務焉。
第貳場
論
聖人至虛至明。
詔誥表内科一道。
translation_en:
…the thirty-second year of Duke Zhao.
In spring, men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song. The fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit. The twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke himself arrived at Jiagu [?]. The tenth year of Duke Ding.

Record of Rites
Five states form a group (shu), with a head; ten states form an association (lian), with a leader; thirty states form a company (zu), with a director; two hundred and ten states form a region (zhou), with a chief.
Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of accord. Those who attain it are honored.
The bringing forth of spring and the growth of summer are benevolence; the gathering of autumn and the storing of winter are righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music; righteousness is akin to ritual.
Virtue is what one attains within oneself. Thus it is said: those in antiquity who studied and practiced the Way sought thereby to realize themselves. Therefore the sages devoted themselves to it.

Second Session
Discourse
The sage is supremely empty and supremely clear-sighted.
One topic from among imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].

translation_en:
Compose a decree in the manner of the Han dynasty establishing provisions to relieve the poor and support the aged. 〔First year of Emperor Wen’s reign.〕
Compose an appointment proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty making Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan.〕

Legal judgments 〔Five cases〕:
Children or grandchildren disobeying instructions and commands.
Officials exceeding the time limit for taking up their posts.
Junior members of a family using property without authorization.
Allowing soldiers to take time off from service.
Military personnel and civilians arranging jointly to bring lawsuits [?].
Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: Among the sages of antiquity who occupied the imperial throne and lived out a long natural lifespan, none equaled Yao and Shun; before them, none equaled the Yellow Emperor. Yet I have sought to understand how the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun attained longevity, without success. When I obtained and read the Three Records (San fen) and the Two Canons (Er dian), what they recorded was entirely these three sages’ reverence …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天卹民之道未嘗言壽豈敬
天卹民之道即所以為壽而壽之道又復有其
說乎已而讀故記乃有述黃帝之所以
壽者其要在守一而處和而堯舜之相
與問對亦復有天德出寧之說焉由是
言之則三聖人之所以壽者誠復有其
指矣毋其道玄妙精微貫通無二而人
莫之測乎諸生其為我解焉今日在
廷諸臣皆以我
===
皇上之壽不獨兼總三聖而直至萬年蓋謂其
道同其
德超也今我
皇上所以敬
天卹民之道凡著之
祀典布之
詔令者業已煌煌燭燭照在耳目間久矣可得
觀焉唯其
聖德之蘊則高遠如
alt_text:
天卹民之道未嘗言壽豈敬
天卹民之道即所以爲壽而壽之道又復有其
說乎已而讀故記乃有述黄帝之所以
壽者其要在守一而處和而堯舜之相
與問對亦復有天德出寧之説焉由是
言之則三聖人之所以壽者誠復有其
指矣毋其道玄妙精微貫通無二而人
莫之測乎諸生其爲我解焉今日在
廷諸臣皆以我
===
皇上之壽不獨兼總三聖而直至萬年蓋謂其
道同其
德超也今我
皇上所以敬
天卹民之道凡著之
祀典布之
詔令者業已煌煌燭燭照在耳目間久矣可得
觀焉唯其
聖德之蘊則高遠如
punctuated: 天卹民之道，未嘗言壽。豈敬天卹民之道，即所以為壽，而壽之道又復有其說乎？已而讀故記，乃有述黃帝之所以壽者，其要在守一而處和。而堯舜之相與問對，亦復有天德出寧之說焉。由是言之，則三聖人之所以壽者，誠復有其指矣。毋其道玄妙精微，貫通無二，而人莫之測乎？諸生其為我解焉。今日在廷諸臣，皆以我皇上之壽，不獨兼總三聖，而直至萬年，蓋謂其道同，其德超也。今我皇上所以敬天卹民之道，凡著之祀典、布之詔令者，業已煌煌燭燭，照在耳目間久矣，可得觀焉。唯其聖德之蘊，則高遠如
translation_en:
…the way of revering Heaven and caring for the people; they never speak of longevity. Could the way of revering Heaven and caring for the people itself be the means of attaining longevity? And might there be a further explanation of the way to longevity? Subsequently, on reading ancient records, I found an account of how Huangdi attained longevity: its essentials lay in preserving the One and abiding in harmony. The questions and answers exchanged between Yao and Shun likewise contain a teaching concerning “Heaven’s virtue bringing forth tranquility” [?]. Viewed in this light, there is indeed a particular purport to the means by which these three sages attained longevity. Might their way be mysterious and subtle, refined and profound, pervading all things as one undivided whole, yet beyond human fathoming? You candidates should explain this for me.

Today, all the ministers at court hold that our Emperor’s longevity will not merely encompass that of all three sages together, but will extend to ten thousand years. Presumably they mean that his way is the same as theirs, while his virtue surpasses theirs. Now, as for our Emperor’s way of revering Heaven and caring for the people, everything embodied in the sacrificial statutes and promulgated in imperial edicts has long shone brilliantly before our eyes and ears, and is available for examination. Only the inner depths of his sagely virtue remain lofty and remote as…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天深默如淵即在
廷諸臣未之能窺而况蒿蓬之士乎然吾竊
以為測天者以景測淵者以意且固有
中之者今爾諸生莊誦我
皇上敬一之箴非一日矣能窺
敬一箴之指則知黃帝之所謂一若和堯舜之
所謂寧矣知一若和與所謂寧則豈不
可以窺
聖德之萬一邪在昔華封之野人眇小耳尚猶
===
致祝堯之詞周公大聖人也思以顯揚
其主君之德則數數稱焉諸生其敬陳
之吾將敬聽之
問錢幣之法先王權度其號令之徐疾而
制上下之用要在上之人操其權以制
下乃其利始流行而不撓是故盜鑄之
禁自昔嚴之矣何漢之賢君乃欲弛其
禁於民而議者捄以七福唐之賢相亦
欲聽其鑄於下而議者規以四美可得

禁於民而議者排以七福唐之賢相亦
欲聽其鑄於下而議者規以四美可得
punctuated:
天，深默如淵，即在廷諸臣未之能窺，而况蒿蓬之士乎？然吾竊以為，測天者以景，測淵者以意，且固有中之者。今爾諸生莊誦我皇上敬一之箴非一日矣，能窺《敬一箴》之指，則知黃帝之所謂一若和、堯舜之所謂寧矣。知一若和與所謂寧，則豈不可以窺聖德之萬一邪？在昔華封之野人眇小耳，尚猶致祝堯之詞。周公大聖人也，思以顯揚其主君之德，則數數稱焉。諸生其敬陳之，吾將敬聽之。

問：錢幣之法，先王權度其號令之徐疾，而制上下之用，要在上之人操其權以制下，乃其利始流行而不撓。是故盜鑄之禁，自昔嚴之矣。何漢之賢君乃欲弛其禁於民，而議者捄以七福；唐之賢相亦欲聽其鑄於下，而議者規以四美？可得
translation_en:
…as Heaven, and as profoundly silent as an abyss. Even the ministers at court have been unable to discern it; how much less could scholars living among the weeds? Yet I venture to think that those who measure Heaven use shadows, while those who sound an abyss use inference, and some certainly arrive at the truth. You students have solemnly recited Our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen) for more than a single day. If you can discern its meaning, you will understand what the Yellow Emperor called “unity and harmony” [?], and what Yao and Shun called “tranquillity.” Understanding these, could you not glimpse even a ten-thousandth part of His Majesty’s sagely virtue? In antiquity, the rustic border guard at Hua was an insignificant man, yet even he offered words of blessing to Yao. The Duke of Zhou was a great sage; wishing to make his sovereign’s virtue manifest, he repeatedly spoke in its praise. You students should respectfully set forth your views, and I shall respectfully listen.

Question: In regulating coinage, the former kings weighed the degree of urgency in their commands and provided for the needs of those above and below. The essential point was that those above should retain control in order to regulate those below; only then could the benefits circulate without disruption. Thus prohibitions on illicit minting have been strict since antiquity. Why, then, did a worthy Han ruler wish to relax this prohibition for the people, while a critic sought to remedy this by presenting seven blessings? And why did a worthy Tang chief minister likewise wish to permit minting among the people, while a critic remonstrated by presenting four merits? Could you…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而陳數與後之識者以爲自昔言貨幣
皆昧要唯兩人頗詳其指信知言否與
裔是論錢法者不爲鮮而儒臣獨取不
惜銅愛工之言爲鼓鑄良法兹兩言較
七福四美論不乖諄與
明興酌輕重之中通錢法濟天下迄於今相
循守不變顧法乆弊生日以蠹壊我
皇上洞察飭振之特鑄新錢兼
本朝前代之適用者布諸民通變捄時天下
===
翕然便之更始矣視昔諸臣所稱說亦
有以兼采行之否與其條列之以酌民
用之宜
問自三代以還其號稱王佐之才者無先
于諸葛孔明乃其相蜀之跡率犁然可
考有作必異有言必偉而宋儒或以偏
才目之何謂乎漢初大功臣蕭何第一
何事高帝常居帷幄中持文墨議論未
嘗有汗馬之勞也而史臣至稱之爲一

明興，酌輕重之中，通錢法，濟天下，迄於今相循守不變。顧法乆弊生，日以蠹壊。我皇上洞察，飭振之，特鑄新錢，兼本朝前代之適用者，布諸民，通變捄時，天下翕然便之，更始矣。視昔諸臣所稱說，亦有以兼采行之否與？其條列之，以酌民用之宜。
問：自三代以還，其號稱王佐之才者，無先于諸葛孔明。乃其相蜀之跡，率犁然可考，有作必異，有言必偉，而宋儒或以偏才目之，何謂乎？漢初大功臣，蕭何第一。何事高帝，常居帷幄中，持文墨議論，未嘗有汗馬之勞也，而史臣至稱之爲一
translation_en:
…can these be enumerated and explained? Discerning men of later times held that all earlier discussions of currency had missed the essentials, and that only these two men had explained its underlying principles in some detail. Was this truly an informed judgment? Subsequently [?], there were no few discussions of monetary policy, yet a Confucian official singled out the statement, “Do not stint on copper; value the workmanship,” as a sound method of minting. Compared with the arguments concerning the seven blessings and the four merits, are these two phrases not more explicit [?]?
When the Ming arose, it struck a balance between monetary appreciation and depreciation, established the circulation of coinage, and provided for the needs of the realm. Its system has continued to be observed unchanged down to the present. Yet, as the system endured, abuses arose, progressively undermining it. Our Emperor perceived this clearly and ordered its restoration, specially minting new coins and circulating them among the people alongside suitable coins of the present and earlier dynasties. By adapting the system to remedy the needs of the times, he has made a fresh start, and all under Heaven have unanimously found it beneficial. Comparing this with what earlier officials advocated, have their proposals also been incorporated and put into practice? Set these out point by point, weighing what is appropriate for the people's needs.
Question: Since the Three Dynasties, among those acclaimed as possessing the talent to assist a true king, none has surpassed Zhuge Kongming. The record of his service as chief minister of Shu is generally clear and verifiable: whatever he undertook was extraordinary, and whatever he said was remarkable. Yet some Confucian scholars of the Song characterized him as a man of limited talents. What did they mean? Among the great meritorious servants at the beginning of the Han, Xiao He ranked first. In serving Emperor Gao, Xiao He regularly remained within the command tent, handling documents and deliberations; he never performed arduous service on the battlefield. Yet the historian went so far as to praise him as a …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
代宗臣何以故始孔明未遇時嘗自比
管樂吾觀孔明之才不謝伊周而顧以
管樂自比豈宋人覩其素許如此而事
功又如彼乃遂爲觀場之見而少之乎
且固有說也高帝差品諸將常取獵事
以白蕭何之功當是時何寵冠羣臣聲
施海内矣意者史臣望其末光以爲竒
絕遂立號宗臣予之邪若不然者必有
說也夫此兩公者皆漢之所稱賢相名
===
大夫也其事功或就或不就天也其大
體有得有不得則人爾不可謂之天也
自今觀之若略其事功而直以才校則
何不逮亮遠甚姑舍其才而直以大體
校則何爲得乎亮爲得乎宋人議論好
窮本偏才之駁不屬孟浪班固撰漢書
務在核實其予何絕甚誠有觀其大者
諸生其深究之夫論人者譬之入寳肆
評賈直也一不得當市者遂用以爲低

評賈貿也一不得當市者遂用以爲低
punctuated: 代宗臣，何以故？始孔明未遇時，嘗自比管樂。吾觀孔明之才，不謝伊周，而顧以管樂自比，豈宋人覩其素許如此，而事功又如彼，乃遂爲觀場之見而少之乎？且固有說也。高帝差品諸將，常取獵事以白蕭何之功。當是時，何寵冠羣臣，聲施海内矣。意者史臣望其末光，以爲竒絕，遂立號宗臣予之邪？若不然者，必有說也。夫此兩公者，皆漢之所稱賢相名大夫也。其事功或就或不就，天也；其大體有得有不得，則人爾，不可謂之天也。自今觀之，若略其事功而直以才校，則何不逮亮遠甚。姑舍其才而直以大體校，則何爲得乎？亮爲得乎？宋人議論好窮本，偏才之駁，不屬孟浪；班固撰《漢書》，務在核實，其予何絕甚，誠有觀其大者。諸生其深究之。夫論人者，譬之入寳肆評賈直也，一不得當，市者遂用以爲低
translation_en:
…an exemplary minister of his age: why was this? Before Kongming found a ruler to serve, he once compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. In my view, Kongming’s abilities were no less than those of Yi Yin and Zhou Gong; yet he compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. Could the Song scholars, seeing both his own longstanding estimate of himself and what he actually accomplished, have formed a mere spectator’s judgment and consequently belittled him? There must surely be an explanation.

When Emperor Gao ranked his generals, he invoked hunting to make clear Xiao He’s contribution. At that time, He enjoyed favor above all the other ministers, and his fame spread throughout the empire. Perhaps the historian, glimpsing the lingering radiance of his reputation, considered him extraordinarily outstanding and therefore bestowed upon him the designation “exemplary minister”? If not, there must be another explanation.

These two men were both celebrated as worthy chief ministers and eminent officials of the Han. Whether their undertakings succeeded or failed depended on Heaven. Whether they grasped the essentials of their responsibilities, however, depended on the men themselves and cannot be attributed to Heaven. Looking back from the present, if we set aside their accomplishments and compare only their abilities, He fell far short of Liang. But if we provisionally set aside their abilities and compare only their grasp of those essentials, was He the one who grasped them? Or was Liang?

Song scholars liked to probe to the roots in their arguments, so their criticism of his limited range of talent was not reckless. In compiling the History of the Han, Ban Gu sought to establish the facts; his exceptionally high praise of He surely reflects an appreciation of his larger qualities. You candidates should investigate this deeply. Judging people is like entering a shop of precious objects and assessing their prices: once an assessment is mistaken, those trading there use it to lower…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
昂可弗慎歟乃若哆口無驗妄施褒抑
而輕揺其筆端即令竒文蔚起主司者
將敝帚視之則何貴焉
問用兵制勝之道在激厲鬪士奮其心然
機宜不越賞罰兩者蓋嘗覽睹古竒傑
操兩者以馭下往往超忽變化改惑觀
聽令人迷所指向莫之測試僂舉𫝊記
中一二籌之彼盜食善馬而賜酒絶飲
卒稱神師而率衆拜禮將冒多矢而賜
===
蓋示旌戚屬失利而揜袂正刑名士違
律而揮涕明法折民匕筯而立誅徇衆
此諸所舉措非恒見所料想外邪邇者
島夷內訌構連深入三吳兩浙之禍殷
矣
聖天子睠懷東南亟圖惟殲滅之乃久不聞滌
海邦之氛以奏功者豈當事之臣牽泥
尋常中未能達古人微眇意指邪夫超
格以懸賞罰則士愛我而不愛身畏我
alt_text:
昂可弗慎歟乃若唦口無驗妄施褒抑
而輕搖其筆端即令奇文蔚起主司者
將漫焉視之則何貴焉
問用兵制勝之道在激厲鬭士奮其必然

聽令人迷所指向莫之測試僂舉其說
中一二籌之彼盜食善馬而賜酒偏飲
卒稱神師而率衆拜禮將冒多矢而賜
===
蓋亦旌威屢失利而擒袂正刑名士違
律而揮淚明法折臂乞貸而立誅徇衆
此諸所舉措非恒見所料想外鄙邇者
島夷內訌構連深入三吳兩浙之禍殷
矣
聖天子睠懷東南亟圖惟殲滅之乃久不聞蕩
海邦之氛以奏功者豈當事之臣牽泥
尋常中未能達古人微眇意指邪夫超
格以懸賞罰則士愛我而不愛身畏我
punctuated:
昂，可弗慎歟？乃若哆口無驗，妄施褒抑，而輕揺其筆端，即令竒文蔚起，主司者將敝帚視之，則何貴焉？

問：用兵制勝之道，在激厲鬪士，奮其心。然機宜不越賞罰兩者。蓋嘗覽睹古竒傑，操兩者以馭下，往往超忽變化，改惑觀聽，令人迷所指向，莫之測。試僂舉𫝊記中一二籌之：彼盜食善馬而賜酒，絶飲卒稱神師而率衆拜禮，將冒多矢而賜蓋示旌，戚屬失利而揜袂正刑，名士違律而揮涕明法，折民匕筯而立誅徇衆。此諸所舉措，非恒見所料想外邪？邇者，島夷內訌，構連深入，三吳兩浙之禍殷矣。聖天子睠懷東南，亟圖惟殲滅之，乃久不聞滌海邦之氛以奏功者，豈當事之臣牽泥尋常中，未能達古人微眇意指邪？夫超格以懸賞罰，則士愛我而不愛身，畏我
translation_en:
…high or low. Can one fail to exercise caution? As for those who speak grandly without evidence, recklessly bestow praise or blame, and wield their brushes lightly, even if remarkable compositions emerge in profusion, the presiding examiners will regard them as worn-out brooms. What value would they then have?

Question: The way to employ troops and secure victory lies in spurring fighting men on and rousing their spirits. Yet the means appropriate to the occasion extend no further than rewards and punishments. In reading about the extraordinary heroes of antiquity, we have seen that, when wielding these two means to govern their subordinates, they often acted with sudden and unpredictable changes, confounding what people saw and heard, so that none could discern or fathom their intentions. Let us enumerate one or two instances from the historical accounts and consider them: wine was bestowed upon those who had stolen and eaten a fine horse; someone abstained from drinking, soldiers hailed him as a divine master, and he led the company in obeisance [?]; a general who had braved a hail of arrows was awarded a canopy as a mark of distinction; a kinsman who suffered defeat was subjected to the prescribed punishment while the commander covered his face with his sleeve; a distinguished man who violated military regulations was punished to uphold the law, though tears were shed; and someone who broke a commoner's spoon and chopsticks was immediately executed as a warning to the troops. Were not all these measures beyond what ordinary experience would lead one to expect?

Recently, the island barbarians have fomented disorder within our borders, joined forces, and penetrated deep inland. The calamity in the Three Wu and the Two Zhe regions has grown grave. The sagely Son of Heaven, solicitous for the southeast, urgently plans their annihilation. Yet for a long time we have heard of no one reporting success in clearing the coastal lands of this pestilence. Could it be that the officials responsible are hampered by adherence to routine and have failed to grasp the subtle intentions of the ancients? For if rewards and punishments are proclaimed beyond the customary rules, the soldiers will cherish me rather than their own lives, and fear me…

而不畏敵此必然之畫也當事者試酌
機激奮之其弗可以厲鬪士使之忘死
生赴敵邪諸生願吐出胸中之竒以裨
平倭之畧
問聖人之教本以捄時行道爲賢而今之
君子固有談古高節獨行之士者此不
可長也其談古高節獨行之士則率稱
引段干木魯仲連之倫焉以爲此二子
者可以亷頑而立懦其說似矣乃或有
===
稱鮑焦爰旌目荆輿顔闔之四人者焉
吾不識四人者之蘊與段魯二子何似
然其行皆過激非人情難繼乃亦博萬
世之名何也嗟乎此亦後世好竒之士
爲之標幟耳不然則四人者皆與孔子
同時孔子著魯論其述賢人君子之行
衆矣然上不挂爰鮑下不引闔輿豈聖
人之論撰顧於亷頑立懦者而屑越邪
亦或其少之也夫高節獨行士之所甚

吾不識四人者之蘊與陵魯二子何似
然其行皆過激非人情難繼乃亦慱蕩
世之名何也嗟乎此亦後世好奇之士

衆矣然上不挂爰鮑下不引闔輿豈聖
人之論撰顧於廉頑立懦者而屑越邪

punctuated:
而不畏敵，此必然之畫也。當事者試酌機激奮之，其弗可以厲鬪士，使之忘死生赴敵邪？諸生願吐出胸中之竒，以裨平倭之畧。

問：聖人之教，本以捄時行道爲賢。而今之君子，固有談古高節獨行之士者，此不可長也。其談古高節獨行之士，則率稱引段干木、魯仲連之倫焉，以爲此二子者可以亷頑而立懦，其說似矣。乃或有稱鮑焦、爰旌目、荆輿、顔闔之四人者焉。吾不識四人者之蘊，與段、魯二子何似？然其行皆過激，非人情，難繼，乃亦博萬世之名，何也？嗟乎！此亦後世好竒之士爲之標幟耳。不然，則四人者皆與孔子同時，孔子著《魯論》，其述賢人君子之行衆矣，然上不挂爰、鮑，下不引闔、輿，豈聖人之論撰，顧於亷頑立懦者而屑越邪？亦或其少之也？夫高節獨行，士之所甚
translation_en:
…and do not fear the enemy. This is a plan certain to produce that result. If those responsible would assess the circumstances and stir the men to action, could they not rouse the fighting men to confront the enemy, heedless of life and death? You candidates are invited to bring forth the extraordinary ideas in your minds to assist the strategy for pacifying the Japanese raiders.

Question: The teaching of the sages fundamentally esteems those who remedy the troubles of their age and put the Way into practice. Yet among today’s gentlemen there are certainly those who speak of men of antiquity distinguished by lofty integrity and independent conduct. This tendency must not be encouraged. Those who speak of such men generally cite figures like Duan Ganmu and Lu Zhonglian, holding that these two could inspire the unscrupulous to become upright and the weak-willed to stand firm. Their argument seems plausible. Some, however, cite the four men Bao Jiao, Yuan Jingmu, Jing Yu, and Yan He. I do not know how the inner convictions of these four compare with those of Duan and Lu. Their conduct was excessively extreme, contrary to ordinary human feelings, and difficult to emulate; yet they too won renown for countless generations. Why is this? Alas! It is merely that men of later ages who delight in the extraordinary have made them into exemplars. Otherwise, since all four were contemporaries of Confucius, and Confucius, in composing the Analects of Lu, described the conduct of so many worthies and gentlemen, why did he mention neither Yuan and Bao nor He and Yu? Could the sage, in his discussions and writings, have slighted and passed over [?] those who could inspire the unscrupulous to become upright and the weak-willed to stand firm? Or was it perhaps that he thought little of them? Lofty integrity and independent conduct are things that scholars find exceedingly…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
難能也然而有聖人為之軌則焉聖人
之出處固不若是之必矣乃若段魯二
子其奇可以扞國家之難望足以寢彊
敵之謀而志在固藏其視聖人之道何
如邪夫持二子以削四子則四子為小
持聖人以削二子則二子又復小矣夫
其遞相不及者何在乎然此四子中且
亦有區別尚費品題未可以一槩量也
諸生其一一第其等焉方今
===
聖明御世山澤之儒苟具一德通一伎者咸来
上謁而誠願自効蓋充滿公車矣然吾
所慮者俗行無名俗事無功將無有好
奇如六子者出乎吾且摘古之非以防
今之趨耳毋曰駢拇而枝贅矣無關世
教也

子其奇可以扞國家之難望足以寢彊

亦有區别尚費品題未可以一槩量也
諸生其一一第其等焉方今
===
聖明御世山澤之儒苟具一德通一伎者咸来
上謁而誠願自効蓋充滿公車矣然吾
所慮者俗行無名俗事無功將無有好
奇如六子者出乎吾且擿古之非以防
今之趨耳毋曰駢拇而枝贅矣無關世
教也
punctuated:
難能也。然而有聖人為之軌則焉，聖人之出處，固不若是之必矣。乃若段魯二子，其奇可以扞國家之難，望足以寢彊敵之謀，而志在固藏，其視聖人之道何如邪？夫持二子以削四子，則四子為小；持聖人以削二子，則二子又復小矣。夫其遞相不及者，何在乎？然此四子中，且亦有區別，尚費品題，未可以一槩量也。諸生其一一第其等焉。

方今聖明御世，山澤之儒，苟具一德、通一伎者，咸来上謁，而誠願自効，蓋充滿公車矣。然吾所慮者，俗行無名，俗事無功，將無有好奇如六子者出乎？吾且摘古之非，以防今之趨耳。毋曰駢拇而枝贅矣，無關世教也。
translation_en:
…difficult to accomplish. Yet the sage provides a standard for such conduct. In taking office or withdrawing from public life, the sage certainly does not insist so rigidly upon one course. As for the two men, Duan and Lu, their extraordinary abilities could have warded off calamities threatening the state, and their prestige could have quelled the designs of powerful enemies; yet they were intent on keeping themselves hidden. How does their conduct compare with the way of the sage? If we use these two men as the measure by which to judge the shortcomings of the other four, the four appear lesser; if we use the sage to judge the shortcomings of these two, they in turn appear lesser. Why does each group fall short of the next? Yet even among those four there are distinctions that still require appraisal; they cannot all be measured alike. You candidates should rank each of them individually.

Now that our sagely and enlightened sovereign rules the world, scholars dwelling among mountains and marshes, provided they possess a single virtue or master a single skill, all come to seek an audience, sincerely wishing to offer their service. They have virtually filled the court’s reception office. Yet my concern is this: ordinary conduct brings no fame, and ordinary undertakings win no distinction—might there not emerge men who seek singularity like those six? I merely single out the errors of antiquity to guard against the tendencies of the present. Do not dismiss this as a webbed toe or an extra finger, a superfluous growth with no bearing on the moral instruction of the age.

text:
第壹場
四書
仁以為已任不亦重乎
潘儴
同考試官教諭栁批脱去凡見而以妙用言
仁子殆識仁體之不匱矣宜錄以式多士
同考試官教諭江批發明任仁之重卓有
定識盖求仁而有得者
同考試官進士羅批萬物一體之意形容
殆盡其以仁自任者耶
考試官侍講袁批詞理淵博是邃於心學者
考試官右諭德王批發揮仁字明盡
大賢即士自任之道以言重欲其知所弘也夫
仁道至大而必欲體之其任不亦重乎士之不
可不弘也以此曾子之意若曰今夫士知任之
為重然後可以語弘知仁之為任然後可以語
重何哉盖仁也者具于一心之微而實冒天下
之道所以立天地者在是所以體萬物者在是

punctuated:
第壹場
四書
仁以為已任，不亦重乎？
潘儴
同考試官教諭栁批：脱去凡見，而以妙用言仁，子殆識仁體之不匱矣，宜錄以式多士。
同考試官教諭江批：發明任仁之重，卓有定識，盖求仁而有得者。
同考試官進士羅批：萬物一體之意，形容殆盡，其以仁自任者耶？
考試官侍講袁批：詞理淵博，是邃於心學者。
考試官右諭德王批：發揮仁字明盡。
大賢即士自任之道以言重，欲其知所弘也。夫仁道至大，而必欲體之，其任不亦重乎？士之不可不弘也，以此。曾子之意若曰：今夫士知任之為重，然後可以語弘；知仁之為任，然後可以語重。何哉？盖仁也者，具于一心之微，而實冒天下之道。所以立天地者在是，所以體萬物者在是。
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Taking benevolence as one’s own responsibility—is this not a heavy burden?”
Pan Rang 潘儴

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Casting off commonplace views, you discuss benevolence in terms of its wondrous operation. You seem to understand that the substance of benevolence is inexhaustible. This deserves to be recorded as a model for the many candidates.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “He elucidates the weight of taking benevolence as one’s responsibility, displaying outstanding and settled discernment. Surely he has sought benevolence and attained something of it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, metropolitan graduate (jinshi): “He describes almost exhaustively the meaning of forming one body with the myriad things. Is he perhaps one who takes benevolence as his own responsibility?”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Expositor: “His language and reasoning are profound and extensive. Here is someone deeply versed in the learning of the mind.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Right Mentor: “He expounds the word ‘benevolence’ clearly and fully.”

The great worthy speaks of the weight of the burden in relation to the responsibility a scholar takes upon himself, wishing him to understand where breadth of spirit is required. The Way of benevolence is supremely great, yet one must seek to embody it: is this responsibility not heavy? This is why a scholar cannot do without breadth of spirit. Master Zeng’s meaning is as if he said: Only when a scholar knows that his responsibility is heavy can one speak to him of breadth of spirit; only when he knows that benevolence is his responsibility can one speak to him of its weight. Why is this? Benevolence is a Way contained within the subtle recesses of a single mind, yet it truly encompasses all under Heaven. Herein lies that by which Heaven and Earth are established; herein lies that by which one forms a single body with the myriad things…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
此其道甚大而用力甚難也彼爲士者可但已
乎蓋行仁固難而君子則先其難者也必也奮
不讓之志而向往之必決由所能而達之于所
不能未嘗畏其難而中止焉仁道固大而君子
則務其大者也必也勵不息之强而率履之必
周以所及而推之于所不及未嘗諉諸大而畧
之焉道之所在則爲天地立極凡天之所以與
我而我之所以善事乎天者蓋無所不盡其心
矣位之所在則爲萬物立命凡物之所以責成
===
于我而我之可以曲成乎物者蓋無所不用其
力矣夫士之以仁自任如此可不謂之重乎蓋
一物一理仁之散殊也舉一物者亦可以言任
不可以言重參天參地仁之全功也舉全功者
乃可以盡仁而士之任始重矣通天地以爲一
體是以一體而負天地矣非合無疆以爲德者
則莫能勝也會萬物以爲一身是以一身而載
萬物矣非包四海以爲量者亦何可當也士而
知此則知所以弘知所以弘則可以體仁而任

punctuated: 此其道甚大，而用力甚難也。彼爲士者可但已乎？蓋行仁固難，而君子則先其難者也。必也奮不讓之志而向往之，必決由所能而達之于所不能，未嘗畏其難而中止焉。仁道固大，而君子則務其大者也。必也勵不息之强而率履之，必周以所及而推之于所不及，未嘗諉諸大而畧之焉。道之所在，則爲天地立極，凡天之所以與我而我之所以善事乎天者，蓋無所不盡其心矣。位之所在，則爲萬物立命，凡物之所以責成于我而我之可以曲成乎物者，蓋無所不用其力矣。夫士之以仁自任如此，可不謂之重乎？蓋一物一理，仁之散殊也，舉一物者亦可以言任，不可以言重。參天參地，仁之全功也，舉全功者乃可以盡仁，而士之任始重矣。通天地以爲一體，是以一體而負天地矣，非合無疆以爲德者則莫能勝也。會萬物以爲一身，是以一身而載萬物矣，非包四海以爲量者亦何可當也？士而知此，則知所以弘；知所以弘，則可以體仁而任
translation_en:
…Thus this Way is exceedingly great, and putting forth the effort it requires is exceedingly difficult. Can one who is a scholar simply desist? Practicing benevolence is indeed difficult, but the gentleman puts its difficulties first. He must rouse a resolve that yields to no one and aspire toward it; he must resolutely proceed from what he can do to attain what he cannot yet do, never stopping midway out of fear of its difficulty. The Way of benevolence is indeed great, but the gentleman devotes himself to its greatness. He must exert unceasing strength to follow it in practice; he must encompass what lies within his reach and extend this to what lies beyond it, never using its greatness as an excuse to neglect it. Wherever the Way is concerned, he establishes the supreme standard for Heaven and Earth: in all that Heaven has bestowed upon him and all the ways in which he can serve Heaven well, he fully devotes his heart. Wherever his position is concerned, he establishes the vital destiny of the myriad things: in all that they look to him to accomplish and all the ways in which he can bring each to fulfillment according to its particular nature, he exerts his strength to the utmost. When a scholar takes benevolence as his own responsibility in this way, can that responsibility fail to be called weighty?

Each thing and each principle are distinct manifestations of benevolence. To take up a single thing may be called a responsibility, but it cannot be called weighty. To stand alongside Heaven and Earth is the complete achievement of benevolence. Only by undertaking this complete achievement can one fully realize benevolence, and only then does the scholar’s responsibility become weighty. To unite with Heaven and Earth as one body is to bear Heaven and Earth with that one body; only one whose virtue accords with their boundlessness can sustain this. To bring the myriad things together as one person is to carry the myriad things with that one person; unless one’s capacity encompasses the Four Seas, how can one bear it? If a scholar understands this, he understands how to be broad in resolve; understanding how to be broad in resolve, he can embody benevolence and shoulder…

text:
重斯無愧于爲士矣抑是道也唯伊尹可以當
之一夫不獲乃曰時予之辜非任歟思天下之
民皆欲其被堯舜之澤焉非仁歟而不懾不沮
與湯一德非弘歟此阿衡之所以爲賢而相道
之所以光也不獨伊尹即周公亦然無逸可以
觀仁赤舄可以觀弘君子合二公之事而並論

人所歸壽者天所與然皆德之固有者也大舜
德隆而福聚則天且弗違而況於人乎此名壽
punctuated:
重，斯無愧于爲士矣。抑是道也，唯伊尹可以當之。一夫不獲，乃曰：「時予之辜。」非任歟？思天下之民，皆欲其被堯舜之澤焉，非仁歟？而不懾不沮，與湯一德，非弘歟？此阿衡之所以爲賢，而相道之所以光也。不獨伊尹，即周公亦然。《無逸》可以觀仁，赤舄可以觀弘。君子合二公之事而並論焉，則知曽子之言固萬世大臣之準也。
必得其名，必得其壽。
柴淶
同考試官教諭沈批：天人相與之際，人所難言，子獨于必理說得明盡，豈貫天人之學者邪？
同考試官教諭張批：說名壽處，塲中鮮有及者。
考試官侍講袁批：辭意當雅，可誦。
考試官右諭德王批：迥異衆作，錄之。
《中庸》著聖君之斂福，而天人不能違也。夫名者，人所歸；壽者，天所與。然皆德之固有者也。大舜德隆而福聚，則天且弗違，而况於人乎？此名壽
translation_en:
…the responsibility is weighty; thus one may be worthy of being a scholar. Yet only Yi Yin could fully exemplify this Way. If even one person failed to obtain his due, he would say, “This is my fault.” Was this not taking responsibility? He thought of the people throughout the realm and wished them all to receive the beneficence of Yao and Shun. Was this not benevolence? Undaunted and undiscouraged, he shared one virtue with Tang. Was this not breadth of spirit? This is what made the Aheng, Yi Yin, worthy, and what brought lustre to the Way of the chief minister. Nor was this true only of Yi Yin: the Duke of Zhou was likewise. In “Against Ease” one may see his benevolence; in his red ceremonial shoes one may see his breadth of spirit. If a gentleman considers the deeds of these two lords together, he will recognize that Zengzi’s words are indeed a standard for great ministers for all ages.
“He will surely obtain his renown; he will surely obtain his longevity.”
Chai Lai 柴淶
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The interaction between Heaven and humanity is something people find difficult to discuss. You alone have explained clearly and fully the principle of inevitability. Can it be that your learning comprehends both Heaven and humanity?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Few in the examination hall can match the passages explaining renown and longevity.”
Comment by Examiner Yuan, Expositor: “The wording and ideas are fitting and elegant, worthy of recitation.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Right Mentor: “Distinctly different from the other compositions. Include it in the record.”
The Doctrine of the Mean makes clear that the sage ruler gathers blessings and that neither Heaven nor humanity can contravene this. Renown is what people accord him; longevity is what Heaven grants him. Yet both are inherent in virtue. The great Shun’s virtue was lofty and his blessings accumulated: if even Heaven would not contravene this, how much less would humanity? This renown and longevity…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之所必得也吾夫子賛舜孝之大而推言之若
曰聖人德體天下之全則福斂天下之備大舜
之所履豈惟祿位之俱造已耶何者帝王德至
於人則萬邦愛戴於是乎有無窮之名然名在
於人雖聖人亦不能必人之我歸其在於舜則
可得而必之人不得而與之吾見德音孔昭觀
諸在朝而賡歌興令聞不已觀諸在野而頌聲
作自玄德之聞以達於四方之風動自重華之
協以及於四夷之來王莫非名也莫非舜之所
===
可必也是其至德光輝充塞天地則聲名洋溢
將天地為昭焉矣大舜之名其冠乎羣倫有如
此帝王德至於天則上帝敷錫於是乎有無窮
之壽然壽出於天雖聖人亦不能必天之我與
其在於舜則可得而必之天不得而愛之吾見
永錫難老而乂道以成化多歷年所而無疆以
配天由授曆之始以引於撫運之靈長由陟位
之初以臻於耄期之悠遠莫非壽也莫非舜之
所可必也是其神聖精誠蟠際宇宙則壽祺永

punctuated: 之所必得也。吾夫子賛舜孝之大而推言之，若曰：「聖人德體天下之全，則福斂天下之備。大舜之所履，豈惟祿位之俱造已耶？何者？帝王德至於人，則萬邦愛戴，於是乎有無窮之名。然名在於人，雖聖人亦不能必人之我歸。其在於舜，則可得而必之，人不得而與之。吾見德音孔昭，觀諸在朝而賡歌興；令聞不已，觀諸在野而頌聲作。自玄德之聞，以達於四方之風動；自重華之協，以及於四夷之來王，莫非名也，莫非舜之所可必也。是其至德光輝充塞天地，則聲名洋溢，將天地為昭焉矣。大舜之名，其冠乎羣倫有如此。帝王德至於天，則上帝敷錫，於是乎有無窮之壽。然壽出於天，雖聖人亦不能必天之我與。其在於舜，則可得而必之，天不得而愛之。吾見永錫難老，而乂道以成化；多歷年所，而無疆以配天。由授曆之始，以引於撫運之靈長；由陟位之初，以臻於耄期之悠遠，莫非壽也，莫非舜之所可必也。是其神聖精誠蟠際宇宙，則壽祺永
translation_en:
…is why he was certain to obtain fame and longevity. Our Master praised the greatness of Shun’s filial piety and extended his argument, as if to say: “When a sage’s virtue embodies all that is complete under Heaven, his blessings gather all that is abundant under Heaven. Could what the great Shun attained have amounted merely to the attainment of both emolument and rank? Why is this so? When an emperor’s virtue reaches the people, the myriad states love and uphold him, and thus he gains boundless fame. Yet fame rests with others: even a sage cannot ensure that others will turn to him. In Shun’s case, however, it could be assured; it was not for others to bestow it upon him. I see his virtuous renown shining brightly: look among those at court, and songs arise in answering verses. His excellent reputation never ceases: look among those in the countryside, and voices rise in praise. From the recognition of his profound virtue to the stirring of the four quarters as if by the wind; from his matching the successive brilliance of his predecessor to the coming of the peoples of the four outer regions to acknowledge his sovereignty—all was fame, and all was something Shun could be certain of. Thus the radiance of his consummate virtue filled Heaven and Earth, and his renown spread everywhere, shining together with Heaven and Earth. Such was the great Shun’s fame, surpassing all his peers.

“When an emperor’s virtue reaches Heaven, the Lord on High bestows blessings abundantly, and thus he gains boundless longevity. Yet longevity comes from Heaven: even a sage cannot ensure that Heaven will grant it to him. In Shun’s case, however, it could be assured; Heaven could not withhold it. I see him granted enduring freedom from the infirmities of age, while his way of governing brought about transforming influence; he lived through many years, his boundlessness matching Heaven. From the beginning, when he received the calendar, his long and auspicious tenure in command of the age unfolded; from his first ascent to the throne, he reached the distant span of venerable old age. All was longevity, and all was something Shun could be certain of. Thus his sagely, divine, and perfect sincerity extended to the utmost bounds of the universe, and the blessing of his longevity endured…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
介將宇宙與存焉矣大舜之壽其出乎庶物有
如此是則舜不必名也而名必集亦不必壽也
而壽必隆則其福之無不備者一德之所有耳
曷常以已與之哉雖然名壽一也不可以異觀
蓋名發於外德之華也壽凝於中德之精也然
壽非名不彰名非壽不永則其原出於一而其
機又相須矣古之聖人未有不兼所得者而惟
舜際堯禹之盛履天地之中極治之化迫邁千
古此夫子所以特賛而亟稱之也中庸以明道
===
之費隱至哉
以德服人者中心悅而誠服也如七十子
之服孔子也詩云自西自東自南自北
無思不服此之謂也
鄭時平

宜錄以式

同考試官進士劉　批　是善形容王道者

punctuated:
介，將宇宙與存焉矣。大舜之壽，其出乎庶物有如此。是則舜不必名也，而名必集；亦不必壽也，而壽必隆。則其福之無不備者，一德之所有耳，曷常以已與之哉？雖然，名壽一也，不可以異觀。蓋名發於外，德之華也；壽凝於中，德之精也。然壽非名不彰，名非壽不永，則其原出於一，而其機又相須矣。古之聖人未有不兼所得者，而惟舜際堯禹之盛，履天地之中，極治之化，迫邁千古。此夫子所以特賛而亟稱之也。《中庸》以明道之費隱，至哉！

以德服人者，中心悅而誠服也，如七十子之服孔子也。《詩》云：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」此之謂也。

鄭時平

同考試官教諭丁批：「王伯之辨，在誠偽之間。子於王者感人處，發揮明鬯，足占辨志之學矣。」

同考試官進士劉批：「是善形容王道者，宜錄以式。」
translation_en:
…bestowed, enduring together with the cosmos. Such was the extent to which the great Shun’s longevity surpassed that of other beings. Thus Shun did not seek fame, yet fame necessarily gathered about him; nor did he seek longevity, yet his longevity necessarily increased. His blessings lacked nothing: all belonged to his virtue alone. When did he ever contribute to them through his own contrivance [?]? Nevertheless, fame and longevity are one and cannot be regarded separately. Fame manifests outwardly and is the flowering of virtue; longevity gathers inwardly and is the essence of virtue. Yet without fame, longevity is not illustrious; without longevity, fame does not endure. Their source is therefore one, and their workings are mutually dependent. None of the ancient sages failed to obtain both. Shun alone, however, stood amid the flourishing ages of Yao and Yu, occupied the central position between Heaven and Earth, and brought the transforming influence of good government to its utmost, rivaling and surpassing all ages. This is why the Master especially praised him and repeatedly spoke of him with admiration. The Doctrine of the Mean thereby illuminates the Way’s pervasive operation and hidden subtlety. How consummate!

“Those who win people’s submission through virtue receive their heartfelt delight and sincere submission, as the seventy disciples submitted to Confucius. The Book of Odes says: ‘From the west and from the east, from the south and from the north, none thought of withholding submission.’ This is what it means.”

Zheng Shiping.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor: “The distinction between the true king and the hegemon lies in sincerity versus pretense. Your exposition of how a true king moves people is lucid and fully developed, sufficient to reveal your learning in discerning the proper direction of the will.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi): “This ably portrays the Kingly Way. It should be recorded as a model.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍講袁批〔王道服人在誠是作得之〕
考試官右諭德王批〔說悅即誠良是〕
大賢言王道感人之誠而必兩有以明之也蓋
王道不外乎一誠也上以誠感下以誠應是豈
伯者之所能及哉孟子申明王伯之辨蓋如此
今夫至不容偽者人之心至不易得者人之悅
唯伯者無以致其悅斯不能服其心矣彼王者
之於天下也其行德也以盡道也而非以市私
恩也以盡分也而非以要人心也然而天下之
===
人皆服焉者其中心悅也彼人情莫不有好而
吾與之聚則凡人之得遂其好者自不能舍其
所好而他有所適矣人情莫不有惡而吾勿以
施則凡人之得違其惡者自不能安于所惡而
唯好是從矣蓋吾之所以行德者誠以行之也
而人之所以服德者亦誠以服之也獨不觀諸
孔子乎孔子當春秋之末造羣七十子而講學
于洙泗之上也特以明道統之傳而已固非必
人人之皆服于我也而七十子之徒罔不悅夫

punctuated:
考試官侍講袁批〔王道服人在誠，是作得之。〕
考試官右諭德王批〔說悅即誠，良是。〕
大賢言王道感人之誠，而必兩有以明之也。蓋王道不外乎一誠也，上以誠感，下以誠應，是豈伯者之所能及哉？孟子申明王伯之辨，蓋如此。
今夫至不容偽者，人之心；至不易得者，人之悅。唯伯者無以致其悅，斯不能服其心矣。彼王者之於天下也，其行德也，以盡道也，而非以市私恩也；以盡分也，而非以要人心也。然而天下之人皆服焉者，其中心悅也。彼人情莫不有好，而吾與之聚，則凡人之得遂其好者，自不能舍其所好而他有所適矣。人情莫不有惡，而吾勿以施，則凡人之得違其惡者，自不能安于所惡而唯好是從矣。蓋吾之所以行德者，誠以行之也；而人之所以服德者，亦誠以服之也。
獨不觀諸孔子乎？孔子當春秋之末造，羣七十子而講學于洙泗之上也，特以明道統之傳而已，固非必人人之皆服于我也。而七十子之徒罔不悅夫
translation_en:
Examiner Yuan, Expositor, comments: 〔“The kingly way wins people’s submission through sincerity. This composition grasps that point.”〕
Examiner Wang, Right Mentor, comments: 〔“To explain delight as sincerity is indeed correct.”〕
The great worthy speaks of the sincerity with which the kingly way moves people, and necessarily elucidates it on both sides. For the kingly way amounts to nothing beyond sincerity alone: those above move others through sincerity, and those below respond with sincerity. How could a hegemon attain this? Such is how Mengzi clarifies the distinction between kings and hegemons.
Now, nothing admits of falsity less than the human heart, and nothing is harder to obtain than people’s delight. Precisely because a hegemon has no means of bringing about that delight, he cannot win their hearts’ submission. In his dealings with the world, a true king practices virtue to fulfill the Way, rather than to purchase allegiance through personal favors; to fulfill his duty, rather than to capture people’s hearts. Yet the reason all people under Heaven submit to him is that they delight in him in their inmost hearts. Everyone has things they desire. If I gather these for them, then all who thereby attain what they desire will naturally be unable to abandon what they love and turn elsewhere. Everyone has things they dislike. If I refrain from imposing these upon them, then all who thereby escape what they dislike will naturally be unable to rest content with what they dislike, and will follow only what they love. Thus, when I practice virtue, I do so sincerely; and when people submit to virtue, they likewise do so sincerely.
Have we not seen this in Kongzi? At the close of the Spring and Autumn period, Kongzi gathered the seventy disciples and taught on the banks of the Zhu and Si rivers, solely to elucidate the transmission of the succession of the Way. He certainly did not insist that everyone must submit to him. Yet among the seventy disciples there were none who did not delight in the Master…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
子之道者有步亦步有趨亦趨而莫或違焉一
誠之所爲耳是誠也即人之服王者之心也故
觀于孔子而王道可知矣又不觀諸詩乎詩言
武王當鎬京之既宅從羣臣而行禮于辟雝之
上也特以敷文教之端而已固非必天下之皆
服于我也而天下之人靡不悅聖人之教者自
西自東自南自北而無思不服焉一誠之所爲
耳是誠也即人之服王者之驗也故觀于詩而
王道可徵矣然則誠也者王道之本其幾始于
===
一念之微而其効極于天下之大王天下者亦
慎其幾而已矣夫所謂慎幾者辨志之謂也志
仁義王也利仁義伯也非王也非以仁義爲利
王也迨其終也仁義効而睟色動怠心作非王
也伯也所謂差之毫釐謬以千里者也不可不
察也大學論治平之道而首之以誠意要之以
慎獨意正謂此西山真氏嘗衍其義以進講焉
蓋將致主于王道而先其幾也吁賢者之事君
固如此

punctuated: 子之道者，有步亦步，有趨亦趨，而莫或違焉，一誠之所爲耳。是誠也，即人之服王者之心也。故觀于孔子，而王道可知矣。又不觀諸詩乎？詩言武王當鎬京之既宅，從羣臣而行禮于辟雝之上也，特以敷文教之端而已，固非必天下之皆服于我也。而天下之人靡不悅聖人之教者，自西自東，自南自北，而無思不服焉，一誠之所爲耳。是誠也，即人之服王者之驗也。故觀于詩，而王道可徵矣。然則誠也者，王道之本，其幾始于一念之微，而其効極于天下之大。王天下者，亦慎其幾而已矣。夫所謂慎幾者，辨志之謂也。志仁義，王也；利仁義，伯也，非王也。非以仁義爲利，王也；迨其終也，仁義効而睟色動、怠心作，非王也，伯也。所謂差之毫釐，謬以千里者也，不可不察也。《大學》論治平之道，而首之以誠意，要之以慎獨，意正謂此。西山真氏嘗衍其義以進講焉，蓋將致主于王道而先其幾也。吁！賢者之事君，固如此。
translation_en:
…the Master's Way: when he walked, they too walked; when he quickened his pace, they too quickened theirs, and none departed from him. This was the work of sincerity alone. Such sincerity is precisely the heart with which people submit to a true king. Thus, by considering Confucius, we can understand the Kingly Way.

Have you not also considered the Book of Odes? The Odes tell how King Wu, after establishing his residence at Haojing, performed rites with his assembled ministers in the Biyong ceremonial hall. His purpose was simply to initiate the spread of civil instruction; he certainly did not insist that everyone under Heaven submit to him. Yet none among the people under Heaven failed to delight in the sage's teaching: from west and east, from south and north, none thought of withholding submission. This was the work of sincerity alone. Such sincerity is precisely the evidence of people's submission to a true king. Thus, by considering the Odes, we can verify the Kingly Way.

Sincerity, then, is the foundation of the Kingly Way. Its incipient stirrings begin in the subtlety of a single thought, while its effects extend to the vastness of all under Heaven. One who would rule all under Heaven as a true king need only attend carefully to these beginnings. Attending carefully to beginnings means discerning one's purpose. To set one's purpose on benevolence and righteousness is to be a true king; to use benevolence and righteousness for advantage is to be a hegemon, not a true king. To refrain from treating benevolence and righteousness as a source of advantage is kingly. Yet if, in the end, once benevolence and righteousness have produced results, a radiant expression appears [?] and a lax disposition arises, this is no longer kingly but hegemonic. This is what is meant by a discrepancy of a hair's breadth leading to an error of a thousand li. It must be scrutinized.

In discussing the way to govern the state and bring peace to all under Heaven, the Great Learning begins with making the intentions sincere and takes vigilance when alone as its essential principle. Surely this is precisely what it means. Master Zhen of Xishan once elaborated this meaning and presented it in lectures to the ruler, intending to lead his sovereign to the Kingly Way by first attending to its incipient stirrings. Ah! Such indeed is the way a worthy man serves his ruler.

translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Those above and below interact, and their purposes are one.”

Chai Lai

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “The implications of its reasoning are profound and enduring; its language and ideas are pure and elegant. The meaning of mutual trust between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers extends beyond the words themselves. Worthy of inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates the meaning of those above and below sharing one purpose, vividly displaying an atmosphere of peace and harmony. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Examiner Yuan, Expositor, comments: “Its meaning rewards prolonged reflection: an excellent composition.”

Examiner Wang, Right Mentor, comments: “It gets to the heart of the matter.”

By observing the utmost mutual trust between ruler and ministers, one can understand the peace of human relations. Ruler and ministers stand in a relationship defined by their respective stations; yet their purposes command each other’s trust. This cannot be achieved without interaction between those above and below. Is this not what constitutes peace in human relations? I take the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments to be this: a ruler aspires to bring order to all under Heaven, but without ministers he has no means of accomplishing this. Ministers aspire to establish great achievements throughout the realm, but without a ruler they have no means of fulfilling their wishes. Thus ruler and ministers depend upon one another to realize their purposes and must not be divided. If their purposes differ, it is simply because those above and below do not interact.

Now the hexagram Peace (Tai) is formed by combining Qian and Kun. With Qian above and Kun below [?], the ruler, recognizing that although the minister’s position is lowly, he bears responsibility for bringing undertakings to completion on the ruler’s behalf, must not remain aloof…

text:
也虚心以逮下勢位不得而拘之焉爲之臣者
以君道宜尊而有忘勢之誠不可負也傾心以
奉上形迹不得而間之焉夫上下之交如此其
志烏有不同者哉吾知勢位之既忘則道心爲
之自通君欲舉之固臣所不欲廢者也形迹之
既泯則誠意爲之自孚臣欲獻之固君所不欲
替者也以參贊天地爲極功君之所以爲期者
此也臣之所以爲期者亦此也未始相謀而默
與之相契蓋有異體而同神者矣以左右斯民
===
爲能事臣之所以爲念者此也君之所以爲念
者亦此也未始相徇而適與之相符蓋有異位
而同情者矣是則惟臣從欲君不疑于其臣惟
君從好臣亦不疑于其君何交之不可久而泰
之不可保哉抑是道也虞廷之君臣蓋有之矣
觀其都俞吁咈未言而信其志不謂同乎然交
相責難之意未嘗不寓于賡歌之中此乃所以
爲保泰之道也嗣是而成周其君臣之相與彌
篤而相戒彌切故宇宙泰和與虞廷比隆焉乃

punctuated: 也，虚心以逮下，勢位不得而拘之焉。爲之臣者，以君道宜尊，而有忘勢之誠，不可負也，傾心以奉上，形迹不得而間之焉。夫上下之交如此，其志烏有不同者哉？吾知勢位之既忘，則道心爲之自通，君欲舉之，固臣所不欲廢者也；形迹之既泯，則誠意爲之自孚，臣欲獻之，固君所不欲替者也。以參贊天地爲極功，君之所以爲期者此也，臣之所以爲期者亦此也，未始相謀而默與之相契，蓋有異體而同神者矣。以左右斯民爲能事，臣之所以爲念者此也，君之所以爲念者亦此也，未始相徇而適與之相符，蓋有異位而同情者矣。是則惟臣從欲，君不疑于其臣；惟君從好，臣亦不疑于其君。何交之不可久，而泰之不可保哉？抑是道也，虞廷之君臣蓋有之矣。觀其都俞吁咈，未言而信，其志不謂同乎？然交相責難之意，未嘗不寓于賡歌之中，此乃所以爲保泰之道也。嗣是而成周，其君臣之相與彌篤，而相戒彌切，故宇宙泰和，與虞廷比隆焉。乃
translation_en:
…He humbly reaches out to those below, unconstrained by power and rank. The minister, recognizing that the ruler’s way deserves reverence and that his sincerity in setting aside distinctions of power must not be betrayed, wholeheartedly serves his superior, allowing no outward formalities to come between them. When relations between superiors and inferiors are like this, how could their purposes fail to accord? I know that once distinctions of power and rank are forgotten, their minds, intent upon the Way, naturally communicate: what the ruler wishes to undertake is precisely what the minister does not wish to abandon. Once outward formalities have dissolved, their sincere intentions naturally inspire mutual trust: what the minister wishes to offer is precisely what the ruler does not wish to discard. To assist Heaven and Earth in their transforming work is the highest achievement. This is what the ruler sets his hopes upon, and what the minister sets his hopes upon as well. Without ever consulting together, they tacitly accord with one another: distinct in body, they are one in spirit. To aid and guide the people is their proper task. This is what occupies the minister’s thoughts, and what occupies the ruler’s thoughts as well. Without ever accommodating themselves to one another, they happen to agree: distinct in station, they share the same sentiments. Thus the ruler follows the minister’s wishes, without doubting his minister; the minister follows the ruler’s preferences, likewise without doubting his ruler. Why should their harmonious relations not endure, and why should the peace of Tai not be preserved?

Indeed, the ruler and ministers at the court of Yu possessed this Way. Consider their exclamations of approval and dissent: they trusted one another before a word was spoken. Could their purposes be said not to accord? Yet the intention to hold one another to demanding standards was always present in the songs they exchanged. This was precisely their way of preserving the peace of Tai. Subsequently, in the perfected Zhou order, the bonds between ruler and ministers grew still firmer, and their mutual admonitions still more earnest. Thus the peace and harmony of the world rivaled the flourishing age of the court of Yu. Only then…

…we thus know that Tai, the hexagram of Peace, speaks of an age governed by sages. A gentleman contemplating it may also envision the spirit of the ages of Yu and Zhou.

“The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation; the great treasure of the sage is called position.”
By Lü Jiong 呂烱.

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “Grand and vigorous, precise and accurate. It fully expounds the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the sage, and deserves to be selected to lead the work of all the candidates.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Concise in expression and abundant in vigor, with thoroughly orthodox argument. A masterpiece.”
Examiner Yuan, Expositor, comments: “It skillfully brings out the profound implications of Heaven, Earth, and the sage.”
Examiner Wang, Right Admonisher, comments: “Refined and penetrating.”

In discussing the Way of Heaven and Earth and that of the sage, the Great Commentary invariably singles out what is most important to each. Heaven and Earth take the generation of things as their heart, while the sage takes the ordering of things as his responsibility. Could what they value most lie anywhere but in generation and position? Without Heaven and Earth, there would be no means to initiate the sage’s governance; without the sage, there would be no means to bring Heaven and Earth’s capacities to fulfillment. These two thus supply one another’s beginnings and completions. Established in their respective places above and below, Heaven and Earth cover and support the myriad things; their capacity is indeed vast beyond all bounds. Yet that by which they extend this capacity to encompass all living beings, keeping the workings of transformation and nurture in ceaseless motion, is called their great virtue. In what, indeed, does this reside? The answer is simply generation. For generating life…

text:
物者天地之心而一元默運固其心之妙于動
靜者也其專而翕也所以育其生之神也而萬
物由之以始其直而闢也所以達其生之用也
而萬物由之以成是雖普萬物而無心在天地
不知有其功而好生之德自有天地以来未之
有改也生非天地之大德而何參賛天地而成
位其中聖人之德盖蕩蕩乎無能名矣然所以
運其德而澤天下使經綸之畧流行而無滯者
則謂之大寶也是果何所在邪曰位而已盖道
===
尊者聖人所貴而至尊無上固其道之藉以大
行者也中天下而立則達之天下而不悖其勢
重者其恩溥也奄萬方而有則推之萬方而皆
準其權一者其教章也是雖有天下而不與在
聖人不以位爲樂而所寶在此自有帝王以来
未之或異也位非聖人之大寶而何由是觀之
則天地所以生聖人者將以弘其道而不匱聖
人所以履天位者唯以憲其道而弗違天地聖
人其合上下而同流者歟雖然天地之道不可

punctuated: 物者，天地之心，而一元默運，固其心之妙于動靜者也。其專而翕也，所以育其生之神也，而萬物由之以始；其直而闢也，所以達其生之用也，而萬物由之以成。是雖普萬物而無心，在天地不知有其功，而好生之德，自有天地以来，未之有改也。生非天地之大德而何？參賛天地而成位其中，聖人之德盖蕩蕩乎無能名矣。然所以運其德而澤天下，使經綸之畧流行而無滯者，則謂之大寶也。是果何所在邪？曰：位而已。盖道尊者，聖人所貴，而至尊無上，固其道之藉以大行者也。中天下而立，則達之天下而不悖，其勢重者，其恩溥也；奄萬方而有，則推之萬方而皆準，其權一者，其教章也。是雖有天下而不與，在聖人不以位爲樂，而所寶在此，自有帝王以来，未之或異也。位非聖人之大寶而何？由是觀之，則天地所以生聖人者，將以弘其道而不匱；聖人所以履天位者，唯以憲其道而弗違。天地聖人，其合上下而同流者歟？雖然，天地之道不可
translation_en:
…bringing things into being is the heart of Heaven and Earth, and the silent operation of the primal unity is precisely the wondrous working of that heart in movement and stillness. In concentration and closure, they nurture the spiritual potency of generation, and through this the myriad things have their beginning; in directness and opening, they give full expression to the workings of generation, and through this the myriad things reach completion. Thus, although they extend to all things without deliberate intent, Heaven and Earth remain unaware of their achievement. Yet their virtue of cherishing life has never changed since Heaven and Earth first existed. What, then, could be the great virtue of Heaven and Earth, if not generation?

Assisting Heaven and Earth in their transforming work and taking his place between them, the sage possesses a virtue so vast that no words can name it. Yet that which enables him to exercise his virtue and bestow blessings upon all under Heaven, allowing his plans for ordering the world to proceed without obstruction, is called his great treasure. Where, indeed, does it lie? In his position alone. For the exaltation of the Way is what the sage prizes, and the position of unsurpassed supremacy is precisely what enables his Way to be put widely into practice. Standing at the center of all under Heaven, he extends it throughout the world without contradiction: his commanding authority makes his beneficence far-reaching. Possessing all regions, he applies it throughout them, and everywhere it serves as the standard: his unified authority makes his teaching manifest. Thus, although he possesses all under Heaven, he remains detached from it. The sage takes no pleasure in his position, yet it is here that his treasure lies; since emperors and kings first existed, this has never differed. What, then, could be the sage’s great treasure, if not his position?

Viewed in this light, Heaven and Earth bring forth the sage so that he may extend their Way without exhaustion; the sage occupies the heavenly position solely to take their Way as his model and never depart from it. Do not Heaven, Earth, and the sage thus unite above and below and flow together? Nevertheless, the Way of Heaven and Earth cannot …

勝原者也但生生爲之本耳若夫雷霆之爲威
霜露之爲慘皆所以成歲功而遂萬物何莫而
非生之道哉聖人者法天以爲治於是德刑賞
罰之政立焉然亦莫非仁也要在納天下於軌
物之中而已至漢董子以陽主于長養陰積於
無用明天之任德而不任刑焉此則依大傳以
立說又欲人君專任德也於乎可謂善言天者
歟亦可謂善告君者歟

勝原者也，但生生爲之本耳。若夫雷霆之爲威，霜露之爲慘，皆所以成歲功而遂萬物，何莫而非生之道哉？聖人者，法天以爲治，於是德刑賞罰之政立焉，然亦莫非仁也，要在納天下於軌物之中而已。至漢董子，以陽主于長養，陰積於無用，明天之任德而不任刑焉。此則依大傳以立說，又欲人君專任德也。於乎！可謂善言天者歟！亦可謂善告君者歟！

書

鄭時平

同考試官教諭丁批：「聖人德化，未易形容。讀是作，則當時化行氣象宛然在目，是邃于經義者。」

同考試官進士劉批：「王化無外之意，發揮殆盡，真傑作也。」

考試官侍講袁批：「昌大。」

考試官右諭德王批：「有氣槩。」
translation_en:
…cannot be exhaustively fathomed. Its foundation is simply the unceasing generation of life. As for the awe inspired by thunder and the severity of frost and dew, all serve to complete the work of the year and bring the myriad things to fulfillment. How could any of these fail to belong to the way of generating life? The sage models his government on Heaven, thereby establishing policies of virtue, punishment, rewards, and penalties. Yet none of these is other than benevolence: their essential purpose is simply to bring all under Heaven within proper norms. In the Han dynasty, Master Dong maintained that yang presides over growth and nurture, while yin is stored away unused, thereby demonstrating that Heaven relies on virtue rather than punishment. He based this argument on the Great Commentary, also wishing rulers to rely exclusively on virtue. Ah! May he not be called one who spoke well of Heaven, and one who counseled rulers well?

Book of Documents

“His influence and instruction reached to the Four Seas”
Zheng Shiping

Associate Examiner Ding, an Instructor, comments: “The transforming virtue of a sage is not easily described. Reading this composition, however, one sees vividly before one’s eyes the scene of that transforming influence at work in those days. This is someone deeply versed in the meaning of the Classics.”

Associate Examiner Liu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), comments: “The idea that the king’s transforming influence excludes nothing is developed almost exhaustively. A true masterpiece.”

Examiner Yuan, an Expositor, comments: “Grand and expansive.”

Examiner Wang, a Right Mentor, comments: “It has force and spirit.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖化大行於天下由治水之功成也蓋水土平
而後敎化洽也自非大禹經理之周焉能盡天
下而達之哉今夫天生神禹造化屬之是故既
有以立經制之功復有以開太平之治何則王
者運皷舞之機而振舉以宣之也有所謂聲焉
闡經綸之蘊而軌範以章之也有所謂敎焉夫
聲敎之弗廣以區畫之未周耳禹也抑洪水而
九州同正庶土而五服定則天地成平氣運際
亨嘉之會風聲由之而不樹矣渾淪再闢人文
===
啓宣朗之期敎化由之而懋昭矣夫聲自我施
若不能必天下之均及也然而惠心惠德莫不
從欲而作孚敎自我立亦不能必萬邦之悉屆
也然而建極歸極罔不徯志而不應東而海隅
則漸焉西而流沙則被焉文命四敷山川不得
而禦之也朔而幽都則暨焉南而明都則及焉
神功遐布風氣不得而限之也是其所施者博
而所濟者衆地有盡而聲無間風行海流與四
旹同運而無方矣曾有一隅之弗至者乎所過

若不能必天下之均及也然而惠心惠德莫不
從欲而作乎教自我立亦不能必萬邦之悉届
也然而建極歸極罔不徯志而丕應東而海隅
則漸焉西而流沙則被焉文命四敷山川不得
而禦之也朔而幽都則曁焉南而明都則及焉
神功遐布風氣不得而限之也是其所施者博
而所濟者衆地有盡而聲無間風行海流與四
時同運而無方矣曾有一隅之弗至者乎所過
punctuated: 聖化大行於天下，由治水之功成也。蓋水土平而後敎化洽也，自非大禹經理之周，焉能盡天下而達之哉？今夫天生神禹，造化屬之，是故既有以立經制之功，復有以開太平之治。何則？王者運皷舞之機而振舉以宣之也，有所謂聲焉；闡經綸之蘊而軌範以章之也，有所謂敎焉。夫聲敎之弗廣，以區畫之未周耳。禹也抑洪水而九州同，正庶土而五服定，則天地成平，氣運際亨嘉之會，風聲由之而不樹矣；渾淪再闢，人文啓宣朗之期，敎化由之而懋昭矣。夫聲自我施，若不能必天下之均及也，然而惠心惠德莫不從欲而作孚；敎自我立，亦不能必萬邦之悉屆也，然而建極歸極罔不徯志而不應。東而海隅則漸焉，西而流沙則被焉，文命四敷，山川不得而禦之也；朔而幽都則暨焉，南而明都則及焉，神功遐布，風氣不得而限之也。是其所施者博，而所濟者衆，地有盡而聲無間，風行海流，與四旹同運而無方矣。曾有一隅之弗至者乎？所過
translation_en:
The sage’s transforming influence spread widely throughout the world because the work of controlling the waters had been accomplished. Only after the waters and lands were brought into order could moral instruction reach everywhere. Had it not been for the thoroughness of the Great Yu’s planning and management, how could it have reached the whole world? Heaven brought forth the divine Yu and entrusted him with the work of creation and transformation. Thus he could both accomplish the establishment of enduring institutions and inaugurate an age of great peace. Why was this so? When a king sets in motion the means of inspiring his people, rousing them and spreading his influence, this is what is called his moral influence; when he unfolds the profound principles of ordering the world and makes them manifest through standards of conduct, this is what is called his instruction. If moral influence and instruction do not spread widely, it is simply because the ordering of the realm is not yet complete. Yu restrained the floodwaters, bringing the Nine Provinces into unity; he put the various lands in order, establishing the Five Zones of Submission. Heaven and earth were thereby brought into equilibrium, and the course of cosmic energies reached a felicitous conjunction of prosperity. His moral influence consequently spread without being deliberately established [?]. The primordial world was opened anew, and human culture entered an age of clarity and enlightenment; moral instruction consequently shone forth with renewed brilliance.

Though I disseminate moral influence, it may seem impossible to ensure that it reaches everyone equally throughout the world. Yet a benevolent heart and benevolent virtue accord with the people’s desires and inspire trust in all. Though I establish instruction, it may likewise seem impossible to ensure that it reaches every state. Yet when the supreme standard is established and people turn toward it, all await the ruler’s intentions and respond [?]. Eastward, it permeated the shores of the sea; westward, it extended to Liusha, the Flowing Sands. His civilizing commands spread in all four directions, and mountains and rivers could not obstruct them. Northward, it reached Youdu; southward, it extended to Mingdu. His divine achievements spread far and wide, and differences of climate could not limit them. Thus what he bestowed was extensive, and those he benefited were many. The land has its limits, but his influence knew no interruption: like the moving wind and the flowing sea, it circulated with the four seasons, unrestricted by place. Was there ever a single corner it failed to reach? Wherever he passed …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者化而所存者神人雖殊而教必達聖作物覩
與天地同流而不匱矣曾有一夫之不獲者乎
是則水土既平賛化育之妙也教化斯洽成彌
綸之能也美哉禹功其萬世永賴者乎抑於此
見大禹之智又可以見帝舜之仁蓋行所無事
智之大也爲天下得人仁之至也智之大則足
以任天下之重而爲生民立命矣仁之至則有
以授天下之聖而爲天地立心矣聖聖相承造
化不以之而斡旋哉噫匪禹之智無以彰舜之
===
仁匪舜之仁亦無以遂禹之智仁智兼濟明良
相與以有成矣此有虞之治後世所以弗可及
也已
亦越文王武王克知三有宅心灼見三有
俊心以敬事上帝立民長伯
包汴

===

俊心以敬事上帝立民長伯
包汴

同考試官進士劉　批　純正充蔚可以式矣
punctuated:
者化，而所存者神。人雖殊，而教必達；聖作物覩，與天地同流而不匱矣。曾有一夫之不獲者乎？是則水土既平，賛化育之妙也；教化斯洽，成彌綸之能也。美哉禹功，其萬世永賴者乎！抑於此見大禹之智，又可以見帝舜之仁。蓋行所無事，智之大也；爲天下得人，仁之至也。智之大，則足以任天下之重，而爲生民立命矣；仁之至，則有以授天下之聖，而爲天地立心矣。聖聖相承，造化不以之而斡旋哉？噫！匪禹之智，無以彰舜之仁；匪舜之仁，亦無以遂禹之智。仁智兼濟，明良相與以有成矣。此有虞之治，後世所以弗可及也已。
「亦越文王武王，克知三有宅心，灼見三有俊心，以敬事上帝，立民長伯。」
包汴。
同考試官教諭丁批：「文武善任，其本在知人，而子能言之，非徒騁詞華者也。」
同考試官進士劉批：「純正充蔚，可以式矣。」
translation_en:
…are transformed, while wherever his influence abides, it works with numinous efficacy. Though people differ, his teaching invariably reaches them. The sage arises, and all look upon him; his influence flows together with Heaven and Earth, inexhaustibly. Could there have been even one person who failed to find fulfillment? Thus, bringing the waters and lands into order reveals the subtle efficacy of assisting the transforming and nurturing powers of Heaven and Earth; making moral instruction prevail everywhere realizes the capacity to encompass and order all things. Magnificent indeed were Yu’s achievements! Surely all generations will rely upon them forever! Here we see not only the wisdom of Yu the Great, but also the benevolence of Emperor Shun. To act without contrivance is the highest wisdom; to find the right man for All-under-Heaven is the utmost benevolence. The highest wisdom enables one to bear the weight of All-under-Heaven and establish the destiny of the people. The utmost benevolence enables one to entrust All-under-Heaven to a sage and establish a heart for Heaven and Earth. As sage succeeded sage, did not the processes of creation and transformation turn through their agency? Ah! Without Yu’s wisdom, Shun’s benevolence could not have been made manifest; without Shun’s benevolence, Yu’s wisdom could not have been fully realized. Benevolence and wisdom aided one another, and an enlightened ruler and worthy minister together brought their work to fruition. This is why later ages could not equal the governance of Shun of Youyu.
“Furthermore, King Wen and King Wu were able to know the hearts of those occupying the three offices and clearly discern the hearts of the outstanding men of those three offices, so as reverently to serve the Lord on High and establish leaders for the people.”
Bao Bian.
Associate Examiner Ding, an Instructor, comments: “King Wen and King Wu were skilled in employing men because, fundamentally, they understood them. You have been able to express this; yours is no mere display of verbal ornament.”
Associate Examiner Liu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), comments: “Pure and correct, rich and abundant: this may serve as a model. …”

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
錄之
考試官侍講袁批說心處有見
考試官右諭德王批能言聖人任人之心
二聖於宅俊之賢知之深而任之重焉盖賢才
者人君所與共天下之理也文武真知而善任
之則其協上下以承休也有以哉周公陳立政
以告成王也及此意曰人君之官人其知之也
不眩而後任之也不惑昔我先王文武其休明
不可紹邪彼登庸於朝而居三事之位者三有
===
宅也是三宅者吾將資之以弘化也不知其心
可乎夫達視其所施彼其敷諸政者可稽也文
武則即其推行之迹以得其心術之微凡其不
愧不怍以靖獻于君者罔不以之而洞見矣夫
豈嘗試之已邪明揚於野而具三事之材者三
有俊也是三俊者吾將資之以熈采也不知其
人可乎夫窮視其所養彼其宣諸言者可睹也
文武則因其擬議之謨而察其由衷之蘊凡其
爲上爲下以効忠於時者莫不以之而畢照矣

二聖於宅俊之賢，知之深而任之重焉。盖賢才者，人君所與共天下之理也。文武真知而善任之，則其協上下以承休也有以哉！周公陳立政以告成王也，及此意曰：人君之官人，其知之也不眩，而後任之也不惑。昔我先王文武，其休明不可紹邪？彼登庸於朝而居三事之位者，三有宅也。是三宅者，吾將資之以弘化也，不知其心可乎？夫達視其所施，彼其敷諸政者可稽也。文武則即其推行之迹，以得其心術之微；凡其不愧不怍以靖獻于君者，罔不以之而洞見矣。夫豈嘗試之已邪？明揚於野而具三事之材者，三有俊也。是三俊者，吾將資之以熈采也，不知其人可乎？夫窮視其所養，彼其宣諸言者可睹也。文武則因其擬議之謨，而察其由衷之蘊；凡其爲上爲下以効忠於時者，莫不以之而畢照矣。
translation_en:
…Include it in the record.
Examiner Yuan, Hanlin Expositor, comments: “The discussion of their hearts shows insight.”
Examiner Wang, Right Mentor, comments: “He succeeds in expressing the sages’ intentions in employing men.”
The two sages understood profoundly the worthy men who held office and those of outstanding talent, and entrusted them with weighty responsibilities. For worthy and talented men are those with whom the ruler shares the governance of the realm. Kings Wen and Wu truly understood them and employed them well: surely this explains how they harmonized those above and below and received Heaven’s blessings! When the Duke of Zhou set forth ‘The Establishment of Government’ to instruct King Cheng, he touched upon this meaning, saying: When a ruler appoints men to office, only after his knowledge of them is free from confusion can his employment of them be free from doubt. Could the splendid enlightenment of our former kings Wen and Wu not be carried on?
Those promoted to service at court and occupying the three high offices were the holders of the three positions. I shall rely on these officeholders to extend the transforming influence of government: could I fail to understand their hearts? When a man holds office, observe what he puts into practice; what he carries out in government can be examined. Wen and Wu accordingly discerned the subtleties of these men’s dispositions and intentions through the traces of their actions. Whatever they did to offer their service conscientiously to their ruler, without shame or remorse, the kings perceived thoroughly by these means. How could this have been merely a matter of trying them out?
Those conspicuously recommended from outside official service, possessing the talents needed for the three high offices, were the outstanding men of the three categories. I shall rely on these talented men to bring lustre to public affairs: could I fail to understand what sort of men they are? When a man lacks opportunity, observe what he cultivates within himself; what he expresses in words can be discerned. Wen and Wu accordingly examined the convictions lodged deep in these men’s hearts through the plans they proposed and discussed. Whatever they did, whether serving above or below, to demonstrate their loyalty in their time, the kings illuminated fully by these means.

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
夫豈面謀之已邪夫知之既深任之有不重哉
蓋人君為天宗子則所以奉天者宜無不盡也
以此宅俊而敬事之與之共天位也精白一心
昭其篤棐之忱焉與之治天職也夙夜匪懈勵
其庶明之翼焉蓋天之所畀於君者咸資宅俊
以代其終矣人君作民元后則所以子民者亦
宜無不周也以此宅俊而長伯之立之以厚民
生也而容保無疆擴吾惠鮮之澤焉立之以正
民德也而教思無窮弘吾怙冒之仁焉蓋民之
===
所望於君者咸藉宅俊以成其能矣夫惟上帝
之事則職業修而所以膺純佑之眷者在此也
夫惟長伯之立則體統正而所以底允懷之休
者在此也此文武克知灼見之效而知恤之實
不亦從可徵哉嗟夫萬化之原涵於一心而帝
王之所以參賛天地左右斯民者咸此心為之
運也周之文武敬止建中心學邃矣故其任賢
圖治必究觀其心而不敢以輕用而當時為之
臣者亦皆殫心靖恭以事其上此所以志同道
