革宿弊而利天下之人民者將不豫爲
今日揚厲邪夫權操於上則博禍除而七福
punctuated: 咸與丕新。頃年以来，照臨幽隱，洞察時奸，知錢貨之行於民者，非復二祖列聖之舊，而殽雜巧偽之徒，私鑄濫惡之物，以阻壞錢法，天下之弊極矣。乃一旦渙號布令，與民更新，特鑄嘉靖通寶，悉復祖宗之制，與前代五銖、開元之輕重適中者兼行於天下。凡民間殽偽之錢，悉罷之。行之未幾，而市肆不易，物貨稱平，朝野之民罔不習而安之，喁喁然欣說而謳吟矣。錢之宿蠹，朝令而夕除；錢之便宜，家喻而戶曉。此誠聖作物覩、人心轉移，而因革損益，燁燁乎宜民之神化矣。丘濬所謂新耳目而通天下之物貨，革宿弊而利天下之人民者，將不豫為今日揚厲邪？夫權操於上，則博禍除而七福
translation_en:
…all shared in the great renewal. In recent years, Your Majesty has illuminated what lay hidden and discerned the malpractices of the age. You recognized that the coinage circulating among the people no longer conformed to the old standards of the two founding emperors and their sagely successors. Those who adulterated metal and devised counterfeits privately cast debased and inferior coins, undermining the monetary regulations. The abuses throughout the realm had reached their extreme.

Then, in a single decisive act, you promulgated an imperial command and issued orders to make a fresh beginning with the people. You specially cast Jiajing tongbao coins, fully restoring the ancestral standards, and circulated them throughout the realm alongside coins of earlier dynasties whose weight was suitable: the wuzhu and Kaiyuan coins. All adulterated and counterfeit coins among the people were prohibited. Before long, the marketplaces continued undisturbed, and commodity prices were said to be stable. People at court and throughout the country all became accustomed to the measure and felt at ease with it, joyfully murmuring their approval and singing its praises.

Long-standing abuses of the coinage were eliminated by evening through an order issued in the morning; the advantages of the coinage became known to every family and household. Truly, when the sage arises, all things behold him, and human hearts are transformed. Through preservation and reform, reduction and addition, this was a brilliantly manifest, wondrous transformation benefiting the people. Qiu Jun spoke of refreshing people's eyes and ears to facilitate the circulation of goods throughout the realm, and abolishing long-standing abuses to benefit its people. Was he not praising the achievements of this very day in advance?

Now, when control rests with those above, widespread calamities [?] are eliminated and the seven blessings…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
集矣法行於民則五不可無虞而四美具
矣銅不之惜工不之愛則錢皆堅厚而民
之奸私阻矣三臣之說悉兼采推行之而
其通變捄時之妙又有非三臣思慮之所
及者是故新錢一出百度需之給廷臣之
俸折軍士之糧佐兵興之急濟司農之匱
足國裕民之道莫有便於此焉愚生樂觀
聖制莫罄名言其將奚以効惓惓之私乎然竊
以為錢者泉也如水行地周流天下而無
===
所不達者也乃今大江以北錢貨阜通而
江以南則有行有不行焉是非果錢之不
可行也特未立法以導之耳倘蒙推廣
聖政明諭而徧曉之令天下皆以銀為權以錢
為使而交易賈售之際非錢不用有不若
者輒以阻壞之罪罪之如此則令出惟行
莫不樂趨而便習之即遐陬窮壤亦將流
布而況邑里市肆間乎此愚生蠡測之見
不敢自黙焉者若以德而立本以義而制

translation_en:
…are gathered. When the law is implemented among the people, the five objections will no longer give cause for concern, and the four benefits will all be realized. If neither copper nor labor is stinted, the coins will all be solid and thick, and illicit practices among the people will be checked. The proposals of the three ministers have all been adopted and put into practice together; yet the ingenuity with which these measures adapt to changing circumstances and remedy the troubles of the age goes beyond anything those three ministers could have conceived. Thus, once the new coins are issued, the many branches of government require them: to pay court officials’ salaries, to commute soldiers’ grain allowances into cash, to meet urgent military expenditures, and to relieve shortages in the state treasury. No means of enriching the state and providing abundance for the people is more advantageous than this.

I, your humble student, rejoice to behold these sagely institutions, whose merits words cannot exhaust. How, then, can I express my heartfelt devotion? Yet I venture to suggest that money, qian, is a spring, quan: like water flowing over the earth, it circulates throughout the realm, reaching everywhere. At present, however, coin circulates abundantly north of the great Yangzi River, while south of the river it circulates in some places but not in others. This is not because coin truly cannot circulate there, but merely because laws have not yet been established to guide its use. If Your Majesty would extend this sagely policy, issuing clear instructions and making it universally understood, everyone throughout the realm could be required to use silver as the standard of value and coin as the medium of exchange, using nothing but coin in buying and selling. Anyone who failed to comply would then be punished for obstructing and undermining the policy. In this way, once an order was issued, it would be carried out; everyone would gladly follow it and grow accustomed to its convenience. Coin would circulate even in remote corners and impoverished regions—how much more so in towns, villages, markets, and shops! 第三問
潘儁
同考試官教諭栁批蕭葛二相美矣卿鮮有
及羣能評隲精詳不可以觀藻鑑邪
同考試官教諭江批蕭稱管之亞匹而葛引
管自比二公未易優劣此策劑量不爽可與尚論古人矣
同考試官進士羅批何在漢唯以能用諸傑號

===
考試官侍講袁批論漢材確有定見録之
考試官右諭德王批主大體論人物最是
人君以大臣之能爲能則心逸而功集大
臣以天下之能爲能則事治而名高名高
則獲在我事治則勞在人功集則獲在上
心逸則勞在下在昔明君之所以撫世賢

translation_en:
…profit, those responsible for affairs have the essential Way of applying the measuring square—judging others by the standard one applies to oneself. What further words need I add?

Third Policy Question
Pan Jun 潘儁

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The two chief ministers, Xiao He and Zhuge Liang, were admirable. Few ministers could match them [?]. Your assessment is precise and detailed: does it not reveal your discerning judgment?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Xiao He was acclaimed as a near equal of Guan Zhong, while Zhuge Liang invoked Guan Zhong as his own comparison. It is not easy to rank these two men. This policy essay weighs them accurately; its author is someone with whom one can discuss the worthies of antiquity.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, metropolitan graduate (jinshi): “Under the Han, Xiao He was acclaimed as an eminent servant of the dynasty simply because he could employ its outstanding men; he was not greatly superior to Zhuge Liang. Your evaluations are clear: no one could surpass you. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Expositor: “His discussion of Han talent shows a firm and definite judgment. Accept him.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Right Mentor: “He assesses historical figures with the larger principles in view. Most sound.”

When a ruler makes the abilities of his great ministers his own, his mind is at ease and achievements accumulate. When a great minister makes the abilities of all under Heaven his own, affairs are well ordered and his reputation rises. When my reputation rises, the benefit falls to me; when affairs are well ordered, the toil falls to others. When achievements accumulate, the benefit falls to those above; when the ruler’s mind is at ease, the toil falls to those below. title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
盡瘁之忠敵愾之氣即鷹揚不過也其詞
感憤其文瑰壯即伊訓不過也又嘗考所
作木牛流馬之制焉其巧通靈其用利捷
即公輸不過也又嘗觀所畫八陣圖焉分
列部署上應天文下合地理即穰苴不過
也孔明奇才也其諸過人者不可勝數然
大率類此矣即就三事而論焉則亮之所
以望抑羣雄名高當世者此也其奉魚水
之歡而不能建一統之業者亦此也何者
===
大體失也今夫人君之于天下也譬之若
天焉宰相者斗杓也百官者四時也天運
則杓轉杓轉則四時行而杓不化而爲四
時也譬之于人若心焉宰相者意也百官
者手足四肢也意聽于心手足四肢聽于
意意不化而爲手足四肢也故天道圜地
道方君主圜臣執方宰相者立于不圜不
方之間所以斡旋四序揮使四體者也若
乃孔明所爲出師表者氣既鷹揚而文復

今夫人君之于天下也，譬之若天焉，宰相者斗杓也，百官者四時也。天運則杓轉，杓轉則四時行，而杓不化而爲四時也。譬之于人，若心焉，宰相者意也，百官者手足四肢也。意聽于心，手足四肢聽于意，意不化而爲手足四肢也。故天道圜，地道方，君主圜，臣執方。宰相者立于不圜不方之間，所以斡旋四序、揮使四體者也。若乃孔明所爲出師表者，氣既鷹揚，而文復
translation_en:
…His loyalty in exhausting himself in service and his spirit of indignation against the enemy were unsurpassed even by the eagle-like prowess of the Grand Preceptor Lü Shang. His words stirred grief and indignation, and his writing was magnificent and forceful: even the Instructions of Yi did not surpass it. I have also examined the design of the wooden oxen and flowing horses he made. Their ingenuity approached the supernatural, and their operation was efficient and swift: even Gongshu could not surpass them. I have also studied the Diagram of Eight Formations he drew. Its divisions, dispositions, and deployments accorded above with celestial patterns and below with the configurations of the earth: even Rangju could not surpass it. Kongming was a man of extraordinary talent. His accomplishments surpassing those of others were beyond counting, but they were generally of this kind. Considering just these three matters, they explain why Liang’s prestige overshadowed the other heroes and his fame towered over his contemporaries. They also explain why, though he enjoyed the happy intimacy of fish and water with his ruler, he could not achieve the unification of the realm. Why? Because he lost sight of the governing essentials.
The ruler’s relationship to the realm may be compared to that of Heaven: the chief councilor is the handle of the Northern Dipper, and the officials are the four seasons. As Heaven moves, the handle turns; as the handle turns, the four seasons proceed. Yet the handle does not transform itself into the four seasons. In comparison with a person, the ruler is like the heart; the chief councilor is the intention, and the officials are the hands, feet, and limbs. Intention obeys the heart, and the hands, feet, and limbs obey intention; intention does not transform itself into hands, feet, and limbs. Thus the Way of Heaven is round and the Way of Earth square; the ruler presides over the round, and his ministers hold to the square. The chief councilor stands between them, neither round nor square, directing the cycle of the four seasons and commanding the four limbs. title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
瑰壯一出則俶儻之士修詞之子皆捫心
退矣木牛流馬之制出則伎匠之徒執斤
錘而求售其巧者皆攦指退矣八陣之圖
出則誦鬼谷之書習黃石之畧者皆批頰
退矣夫使諸技客才人皆退而不敢前引
以為弗如而不肯任則亮不得不勞以故
恒自立于矢石之間事無大小悉决于帳
前課功程罪不爽毫髮是斗杓化而為四
時意化而為手足四肢也事必不可集功
===
必不可就才累之也而大體失也所謂大
體者我無能而無不能也我不足而無不
足也不操鉛槧而天下之文皆吾文也不
事剞劂而天下之巧皆吾巧也不學兵法
而天下之畧皆吾畧也人君執斯道而任
相則爵禄不悖宰相執斯道而柄事則福
澤無窮何以說也漢高帝之起豐沛而定
天下也天下豪傑之士雲附景從日以百
輩來乃拜蕭何為丞相所謂爵禄不悖者

punctuated:
瑰壯，一出則俶儻之士、修詞之子皆捫心退矣。木牛流馬之制出，則伎匠之徒執斤錘而求售其巧者，皆攦指退矣。八陣之圖出，則誦鬼谷之書、習黃石之畧者，皆批頰退矣。夫使諸技客才人皆退而不敢前，引以為弗如而不肯任，則亮不得不勞。以故恒自立于矢石之間，事無大小，悉决于帳前，課功程罪，不爽毫髮。是斗杓化而為四時，意化而為手足四肢也。事必不可集，功必不可就，才累之也，而大體失也。
所謂大體者，我無能而無不能也，我不足而無不足也。不操鉛槧，而天下之文皆吾文也；不事剞劂，而天下之巧皆吾巧也；不學兵法，而天下之畧皆吾畧也。人君執斯道而任相，則爵禄不悖；宰相執斯道而柄事，則福澤無窮。何以說也？漢高帝之起豐沛而定天下也，天下豪傑之士雲附景從，日以百輩來，乃拜蕭何為丞相，所謂爵禄不悖者
translation_en:
…magnificent and powerful. Once it appeared, men of exceptional talent and masters of literary composition all felt their hearts and withdrew. When the design of the wooden oxen and flowing horses appeared, craftsmen who wielded axes and hammers and sought to market their skill all broke their fingers and withdrew. When the Diagram of the Eight Battle Formations appeared, those who recited the writings of Guiguzi and studied the strategies of Huangshi all slapped their cheeks and withdrew. If all these skilled specialists and talented men are made to retreat, not daring to come forward, and acknowledge their inferiority and refuse to undertake responsibilities, then Liang cannot but toil himself. Thus he constantly placed himself amid arrows and stones. Every matter, great or small, was decided before his command tent; he assessed achievements and measured offenses without erring by a hair’s breadth. This is the handle of the Dipper transforming itself into the four seasons, and the will transforming itself into the hands, feet, and limbs. Affairs necessarily could not be brought to completion, nor achievements secured: his talent encumbered him, and the governing essentials were lost.
What are these governing essentials? I have no ability, yet there is nothing I cannot do; I am insufficient, yet there is nothing for which I am insufficient. Without taking up a lead stylus and writing tablet, all the writing under Heaven is my writing. Without working with carving tools, all the craftsmanship under Heaven is my craftsmanship. Without studying military methods, all the strategies under Heaven are my strategies. If a ruler follows this Way in appointing his chief minister, ranks and emoluments will not be improperly bestowed. If a chief minister follows this Way in directing affairs, blessings and favors will be inexhaustible. How can this be explained? When Emperor Gao of Han rose from Feng and Pei and brought all under Heaven to order, the outstanding men of the realm gathered about him like clouds and followed him like shadows, coming by the hundreds each day. He then appointed Xiao He as Chief Councilor. This is what is meant by ranks and emoluments not being improperly bestowed…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也天下既定論功行賞蕭何功第一先封
於是封何爲酇侯食邑八千戶位次居諸
將之上賜劔履上殿入朝令勿趨已又封
其父母兄弟凡十餘人皆食邑有差此所
謂福澤無窮者也自今考酇侯之爲相也
無奇也以運籌決勝不如良之智也以戰
克攻取不如信之捷也以揮霍先登不如
參之勇也以橫行直下不如噲之敢也其
功爲第一者以無智而使智良則良出其
===
智以無捷而使捷信則信見其捷以無勇
而使勇參則參奮其勇以無敢而使敢噲
則噲施其敢而沛公之帝業成焉故未嘗
挽強而曰射取江東者酇侯也未嘗馳駿
而曰踴躍中原者酇侯也何非能踴躍非
能射取諸將之踴躍射取者悉歸之何以
何能使之也取亮較何何木疆人耳出師
二表何不能爲木牛流馬何不能制八陣
圖何不能解獨以無文而用文無制而用

也。天下既定，論功行賞，蕭何功第一，先封。於是封何爲酇侯，食邑八千戶，位次居諸將之上，賜劔履上殿，入朝令勿趨。已，又封其父母兄弟，凡十餘人，皆食邑有差。此所謂福澤無窮者也。
自今考酇侯之爲相也，無奇也。以運籌決勝，不如良之智也；以戰克攻取，不如信之捷也；以揮霍先登，不如參之勇也；以橫行直下，不如噲之敢也。其功爲第一者，以無智而使智，良則良出其智；以無捷而使捷，信則信見其捷；以無勇而使勇，參則參奮其勇；以無敢而使敢，噲則噲施其敢，而沛公之帝業成焉。故未嘗挽強，而曰射取江東者，酇侯也；未嘗馳駿，而曰踴躍中原者，酇侯也。何非能踴躍，非能射取，諸將之踴躍射取者悉歸之何，以何能使之也。
取亮較何，何木疆人耳。出師二表，何不能爲；木牛流馬，何不能制；八陣圖，何不能解。獨以無文而用文，無制而用
translation_en:
…such was the case. Once the realm had been pacified, achievements were assessed and rewards bestowed. Xiao He ranked first in merit and was the first to be enfeoffed. He was accordingly made Marquis of Cuo, with a fief supporting him from eight thousand households, and ranked above all the generals. He was granted permission to ascend the palace hall wearing his sword and shoes, and was exempted from hastening his steps when entering court. Subsequently, his parents and brothers, more than ten people in all, were also enfeoffed, each receiving a fief of a different size. This is what is meant by blessings and bounty without end.
Examining the Marquis of Cuo’s service as chief minister from our present vantage point, we find nothing extraordinary. In devising strategies and securing victory, he lacked Zhang Liang’s wisdom; in winning battles and capturing positions, he lacked Han Xin’s swift effectiveness; in wielding weapons and being first to scale the walls, he lacked Cao Can’s courage; in sweeping forward and taking positions directly, he lacked Fan Kuai’s daring. His merit ranked first because, though lacking wisdom himself, he employed the wise, and Liang contributed his wisdom; though lacking swift effectiveness himself, he employed those who possessed it, and Xin displayed his effectiveness; though lacking courage himself, he employed the courageous, and Can roused his courage; though lacking daring himself, he employed the daring, and Kuai exercised his daring. Thus the Lord of Pei’s imperial enterprise was accomplished. Hence, though he never drew a powerful bow, the man credited with winning Jiangdong by archery was the Marquis of Cuo; though he never galloped on a fine steed, the man credited with charging across the Central Plain was the Marquis of Cuo. Xiao He was not himself able to charge or to conquer by archery. The generals’ charging and conquering were all credited to him because he could employ them.
Compare Zhuge Liang with Xiao He: Xiao He was merely a plain, unbending man [?]. He could not have written the two Memorials on Dispatching the Army; he could not have devised the wooden oxen and flowing horses; he could not have understood the Diagram of the Eight Battle Formations. Yet, though lacking literary ability, he employed those who possessed it; though unable to devise, he employed…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
制不解而用解遂以佐成大業而享有令
名寵冠羣臣而慶流苗裔也由此觀之則
班固以一代宗臣予何者非以何事功謂
也謂其忘己任人恢恢乎有大臣之體也
後世有佩何印綬襲何職事者則撫海內
鎮國家無事他求即此人乃其宗矣宋人
目亮爲偏才者非以事功弗就之謂也謂
其抱才自用不屬之人也役耳目任聰明
屑屑瑟瑟殊異乎混一之規模無內無外
===
之氣象也今夫天下之事一有未治則責
之相社稷之功一有未集則責之相即令
相事事而擘畫之人人而譙聒之懵懵然
用力益勞而取効益遠求之彌切而得之
彌艱故在用人而用人之道又在乎有能
而不能有餘而不足蕭何之驅使諸將也
似于無能而能于諸將疑于不足而足于
諸將彼孔明者有奇而直見其竒耳此竒
者不爲用也此兩公之別也竊嘗觀于孔

目亮爲儒才者非以事功弗就之謂也謂

諸將彼孔明者有奇而直見其奇耳此奇

punctuated: 制，不解而用解，遂以佐成大業而享有令名，寵冠羣臣而慶流苗裔也。由此觀之，則班固以一代宗臣予何者，非以何事功謂也，謂其忘己任人，恢恢乎有大臣之體也。後世有佩何印綬、襲何職事者，則撫海內、鎮國家，無事他求，即此人乃其宗矣。宋人目亮爲偏才者，非以事功弗就之謂也，謂其抱才自用，不屬之人也。役耳目，任聰明，屑屑瑟瑟，殊異乎混一之規模、無內無外之氣象也。今夫天下之事，一有未治，則責之相；社稷之功，一有未集，則責之相。即令相事事而擘畫之，人人而譙聒之，懵懵然，用力益勞而取効益遠，求之彌切而得之彌艱。故在用人，而用人之道，又在乎有能而不能，有餘而不足。蕭何之驅使諸將也，似于無能而能于諸將，疑于不足而足于諸將。彼孔明者，有奇而直見其竒耳，此竒者不爲用也。此兩公之別也。竊嘗觀于孔
translation_en:
…devise them; though unable to understand, he employed those who understood. Thus he helped accomplish the great undertaking and enjoyed an excellent reputation; his favor surpassed that of all other ministers, and blessings flowed down to his descendants. Viewed in this light, Ban Gu’s designation of Xiao He as the exemplary minister of his age referred not to his achievements, but to his forgetting himself and entrusting responsibilities to others: his capacious spirit embodied the character of a great minister. If later generations should include men who wear He’s seal and ribbon and assume his duties, they need look no further for a model in bringing peace to all under Heaven and securing the state: this man is their exemplar. When men of the Song called Zhuge Liang a man of limited talents, they were not referring to his failure to accomplish his undertaking. They meant that he relied on his own talents and employed them himself, rather than entrusting tasks to others. He strained his ears and eyes and relied on his own intelligence, fussing over details with anxious care—very different from the breadth of vision needed to unite the realm, or the spirit that embraces both inner and outer affairs.

Now, whenever any affair under Heaven remains unregulated, responsibility is laid upon the chief councilor; whenever any undertaking for the state remains unaccomplished, responsibility is laid upon the chief councilor. Even if the chief councilor were to plan every single matter and admonish every single person, he would labor on in bewilderment: the more exhausting his efforts, the more remote their results; the more urgently he sought success, the harder it would be to attain. The key, therefore, lies in employing others, and the way to employ others lies in possessing ability yet acting as though unable, possessing more than enough yet acting as though insufficient. In directing the generals, Xiao He seemed incapable, yet through the generals he was capable; he appeared insufficient, yet through the generals he had sufficiency. As for Kongming—that is, Zhuge Liang—he possessed extraordinary talents, but merely displayed those talents himself; such extraordinary talent was not put to effective use. This is the distinction between these two gentlemen. I have ventured to consider the example of Confucius…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
子矣力能舉國門之關而不以力逞懼夫
人之有力者不爲我盡也明能見吳門之
馬而不以明著懼夫人之有明者不爲我
視也博能辨萍實之狀表商羊之異而不
以博衒懼夫人之有博者不爲我告也智
能决拾塵之誣料結纓之禍而不以智名
懼夫人之有智者不爲我察也故其相魯
也一月而功集三月而道行不自聖也不
自聖乃所以爲聖不自賢乃所以爲賢惜
===
哉亮之不察乎此也夫相臣之於天下也
其始而分其任于衆也猶之治絲焉人理
一縷人司一染已而付之機上杼柚既成
則貴人衣之不曰某工之所製也但稱曰
某貴人之衣錦美錦也猶之乘馬焉伯樂
相之王良御之造父驅之貴人乘焉而過
于市市人曰貴人之馬良馬也不問相之
御之驅之者誰也其事治功集君上悅之
而獲有福禄也猶之宴賓焉宴賓者酒人

punctuated: 子矣。力能舉國門之關，而不以力逞，懼夫人之有力者不爲我盡也；明能見吳門之馬，而不以明著，懼夫人之有明者不爲我視也；博能辨萍實之狀，表商羊之異，而不以博衒，懼夫人之有博者不爲我告也；智能决拾塵之誣，料結纓之禍，而不以智名，懼夫人之有智者不爲我察也。故其相魯也，一月而功集，三月而道行。不自聖也，不自聖乃所以爲聖，不自賢乃所以爲賢。惜哉，亮之不察乎此也！夫相臣之於天下也，其始而分其任于衆也，猶之治絲焉：人理一縷，人司一染，已而付之機上，杼柚既成，則貴人衣之，不曰某工之所製也，但稱曰：「某貴人之衣錦，美錦也。」猶之乘馬焉：伯樂相之，王良御之，造父驅之，貴人乘焉而過于市，市人曰：「貴人之馬，良馬也。」不問相之、御之、驅之者誰也。其事治功集，君上悅之，而獲有福禄也，猶之宴賓焉：宴賓者，酒人
translation_en:
…Confucius. His strength enabled him to lift the bar of a capital’s gate, yet he did not flaunt his strength, fearing that others possessed of strength would not exert themselves fully for him. His keen sight enabled him to see the horse at the gate of Wu, yet he did not make a display of his sight, fearing that others with keen sight would not look on his behalf. His extensive learning enabled him to identify the duckweed fruit and explain the portent of the shangyang bird, yet he did not parade his learning, fearing that others with extensive learning would not inform him. His wisdom enabled him to resolve the false accusation concerning the removal of dust from rice and foresee the calamity of tying one’s cap strings, yet he did not seek renown for wisdom, fearing that others possessed of wisdom would not investigate matters for him. Thus, when he served as minister in Lu, achievements were accomplished within one month, and the Way prevailed within three months. He did not claim sagehood for himself. Not claiming sagehood for oneself is precisely how one becomes a sage; not claiming worthiness for oneself is precisely how one becomes worthy. Alas that Liang failed to understand this!

When a chief minister first apportions his responsibilities for the realm among others, it is like preparing silk: each person puts a strand in order, and each oversees a dyeing task. The silk is then placed on the loom. Once the weaving is finished, a nobleman wears it. People do not say that it was made by such-and-such a craftsman; they merely remark, “The brocade worn by that nobleman is beautiful brocade.” It is also like riding a horse: Bole appraises it, Wang Liang handles its reins, and Zaofu drives it. A nobleman rides it through the marketplace, and the people there say, “The nobleman’s horse is a fine horse.” They do not ask who appraised it, handled its reins, or drove it. When the minister’s affairs are well managed and his achievements accomplished, the ruler is pleased with him, and he receives blessings and emoluments. It is like entertaining guests at a banquet: when someone entertains guests, the wine attendant…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
奉觴饔人奉膳鼓瑟吹竽客心甚樂矣明
日不拜樂人者而拜主人主人使之也猶
之治宮室焉大匠為圓必以規為方必以
矩方圓既成則規矩無功而主人謝大匠
曰巧工也及宮室既成邦人相賀不賀大
匠而賀主人主人居之也蕭何有辨于此
故竟以帷幄蒙福孔明不察乎此故迄用
瘁斃此兩公之別也雖然自二表傳而逆
臣懦子讀之骨竦而毛竪自陣圖立即江
===
水泛濫而行次不失焉自牛馬之制出歷
數百歲未有能解其事者此蓋天地之毓
靈孕秀鬼神之託精見異乃生此隆中之
龍耳非庸衆人也顧愚所為扼腕者念其
齎志而終令萬世有憐才之嘆耳抑愚又
有說焉從古以来號稱才士者不可勝紀
然往往不聞道不聞道則才不成不聞道
者何也不學也所謂學者非他也唯在于
忘好惡去巧故釋智術除將迎栖志乎無

奉觴，饔人奉膳，鼓瑟吹竽，客心甚樂矣。明日，不拜樂人者而拜主人，主人使之也。猶之治宮室焉，大匠為圓必以規，為方必以矩。方圓既成，則規矩無功，而主人謝大匠曰：「巧工也。」及宮室既成，邦人相賀，不賀大匠而賀主人，主人居之也。蕭何有辨于此，故竟以帷幄蒙福；孔明不察乎此，故迄用瘁斃。此兩公之別也。雖然，自二表傳，而逆臣懦子讀之，骨竦而毛竪；自陣圖立，即江水泛濫，而行次不失焉；自牛馬之制出，歷數百歲，未有能解其事者。此蓋天地之毓靈孕秀，鬼神之託精見異，乃生此隆中之龍耳，非庸衆人也。顧愚所為扼腕者，念其齎志而終，令萬世有憐才之嘆耳。
抑愚又有說焉。從古以来，號稱才士者不可勝紀，然往往不聞道。不聞道則才不成。不聞道者何也？不學也。所謂學者，非他也，唯在于忘好惡，去巧故，釋智術，除將迎，栖志乎無
translation_en:
…present the wine cups, while the cooks serve the food; zithers are played and mouth organs blown, and the guests are thoroughly delighted. The next day they pay their respects not to the musicians but to the host, for it is the host who has directed them. It is likewise with building a residence. To make a circle, the master carpenter must use a compass; to make a square, he must use a carpenter’s square. Once the squares and circles are finished, the compass and square receive no credit; instead, the owner thanks the master carpenter, saying, “A skillful craftsman!” When the residence is completed, the people of the locality offer congratulations, not to the master carpenter but to the owner, for it is the owner who inhabits it. Xiao He understood this distinction and thus ultimately gained blessings through his work in the command tent. Kongming failed to perceive it and so finally worked himself to death. This is the difference between these two men. Nevertheless, ever since his two memorials circulated, rebellious ministers and cowardly sons have read them with their bones trembling and their hair standing on end. Ever since his battle formation was laid out, even when the river overflowed, its ranks and ordering remained intact. Ever since his designs for oxen and horses appeared, several hundred years have passed without anyone being able to explain how they worked. Surely Heaven and Earth nurtured spiritual potency and excellence, and the spirits lodged their essence and manifested wonders, to bring forth this dragon of Longzhong. He was no ordinary man. Yet what makes me wring my hands is the thought that he died with his ambitions unfulfilled, leaving all subsequent ages to lament his unrealized talent.

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
妄之次游意乎自然之塗如是則無以害
其真而知精知精則知神知神之謂知道
凡彼羣才得道然後廣故知道則萬物畢
聚濶大淵深不可測也性情嚴局無所思
慕不可誘也塵壒超絶中情潔白不可汙
也靈徹貫通比于蓍蔡不可欺也動作當
務與時變化不可窮也得失成敗先幾炳
見不可遹也賢人至前邪夫乗之不可溷
也毁玉爲珉譽蕕爲荃不可誰也夫誰知
===
道則才乃逹才逹則無己無人無内無外
無己則無難舎己無人則無難任人無内
則無醜力不己出無外則無惡功從人立
此學之成也孔明講于寧靜之學蓋嘗聞
道矣又其治蜀也亦嘗開誠心布公道集
衆思廣忠益矣固非用才自見者也而所
就竟若此何也蓋其才焰閃爍如燈之在
帷一開一合時見時藏而不可終遏也以
故觀者疑之疑生懼懼則衆不爲使而事

translation_en:
…the abode of freedom from delusion, and let the mind roam the paths of naturalness. In this way nothing impairs one's authenticity, and one comes to understand the subtle essence. Understanding the subtle essence leads to understanding the numinous; understanding the numinous is what is called understanding the Way. All those various talents become expansive only after attaining the Way. Thus, when one understands the Way, the myriad things gather within oneself: vast and profoundly deep, one cannot be fathomed. With one's nature and feelings strictly ordered, and nothing coveted or yearned for, one cannot be enticed. Transcending worldly dust, with inner feelings pure and spotless, one cannot be defiled. With luminous insight penetrating all things, comparable to divining stalks and tortoise shells, one cannot be deceived. Acting appropriately to the task and changing with the times, one cannot be exhausted. Seeing clearly the first intimations of gain and loss, success and failure, one cannot be deflected [?]. When worthy men come forward and wicked men take advantage of them [?], one cannot be confused. When jade is disparaged as an inferior stone and foul-smelling herbs are praised as fragrant ones, one cannot be… [?]. Whoever understands the Way [?] then brings his talents to full realization. When his talents are fully realized, there is neither self nor other, neither inner nor outer. Without self, one has no difficulty setting oneself aside; without others, one has no difficulty entrusting others with responsibility. Without an inner realm, one feels no shame when the effort does not originate with oneself; without an outer realm, one feels no resentment when achievements are established by others. This is the consummation of learning.

Kongming devoted himself to the learning of tranquillity and surely had heard the Way. Moreover, in governing Shu, he opened his sincere heart, made public the impartial Way, gathered the thoughts of many, and broadened the benefits of loyal counsel. He certainly was not someone who used his talents to display himself. Why, then, did his accomplishments ultimately amount to this? The flame of his talent flickered like a lamp behind a curtain: as the curtain opened and closed, it was now visible, now concealed, yet could never be suppressed altogether. Consequently, those who observed him grew suspicious. Suspicion bred fear; fear meant that the multitude would not serve at his direction, and his undertakings…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
功隳然則君子之學也非聞道之難而體
道之貴蓋自古記之矣
第四問
楊濂
同考試官知縣毛批平倭之畧士子類能
言之然莫可施行此策深探患本其條消弭之術
固有老將所弗及者録之以裨幕中之畫
考試官侍講袁批格外賞罰古人行之今人
昧之夷患乆未殄者坐此子能酌變化之機而確乎
===
可行豈空言而無實用者乎
考試官右諭德王批兵家常用竒勝如子之
言非竒邪可以制島夷矣
善用兵者其操之有機宜而運之有妙用
夫機宜有常形所以立其衡而使人無所
不可知妙用無定迹所以神其術而使人
有所不可測是故兩者迭施則惠行而莫
不忘生威行而莫不忘死蓋下有忘生之
心則愛我而不自愛有忘死之心則畏我

言非奇邪可以制島夷矣
===
善用兵者其操之有機宜而運之有妙用

心則愛我而不自愛有忘死之心則畏我
punctuated:
功隳。然則君子之學也，非聞道之難，而體道之貴，蓋自古記之矣。

第四問
楊濂

同考試官知縣毛批：平倭之畧，士子類能言之，然莫可施行。此策深探患本，其條消弭之術，固有老將所弗及者，録之以裨幕中之畫。

考試官侍講袁批：格外賞罰，古人行之，今人昧之。夷患乆未殄者，坐此。子能酌變化之機，而確乎可行，豈空言而無實用者乎？

考試官右諭德王批：兵家常用竒勝，如子之言，非竒邪？可以制島夷矣。

善用兵者，其操之有機宜，而運之有妙用。夫機宜有常形，所以立其衡，而使人無所不可知；妙用無定迹，所以神其術，而使人有所不可測。是故兩者迭施，則惠行而莫不忘生，威行而莫不忘死。蓋下有忘生之心，則愛我而不自愛；有忘死之心，則畏我
translation_en:
…and achievements come to ruin. Thus, in the gentleman’s learning, the difficulty of hearing the Way is not the chief concern; what matters is embodying the Way. This has indeed been recorded since antiquity.

Fourth Question
Yang Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, District Magistrate: Candidates generally can discuss strategies for pacifying the Japanese pirates, yet none can be put into practice. This policy essay probes deeply into the roots of the trouble. Among the methods it enumerates for eliminating it are some beyond even veteran generals. It is recorded here to aid planning at military headquarters.

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Expositor: Rewards and punishments outside the ordinary rules were employed by the ancients, but people today fail to understand them. This is why the trouble caused by the barbarians has long remained uneradicated. You have weighed the opportunities for adapting to changing circumstances, and your proposals are assuredly practicable. How could these be empty words without practical utility?

Comment by Examiner Wang, Right Mentor: Military strategists regularly win through unorthodox methods. Are not proposals such as yours unorthodox? They could subdue the island barbarians.

Those skilled in warfare have appropriate measures for managing it and subtle methods for putting them into effect. Appropriate measures have a regular form: they establish a standard and leave nothing that people cannot understand. Subtle methods follow no fixed pattern: they make the technique unfathomable and leave something that people cannot predict. Thus, when the two are applied in alternation, benevolence is exercised and all forget concern for their own lives; authority is exercised and all forget fear of death. When those below have a heart that forgets concern for life, they cherish me rather than themselves; when they have a heart that forgets fear of death, they fear me…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而不畏敵吾見將士一心闘氣益倍唯吾
所欲用之雖赴水火可也而何敵之不制
何堅之不瑕何暴亂之不平哉故賞罰者
所持以激厲人心之機宜衡立而無所不
可知者也若屈伸變化使人顛倒皷舞於
其中而不自覺此則非常之妙用制敵之
微權英雄豪傑之士所以陰用而不言而
人亦莫之測者也達於此者可與語兵之
變而知所以運賞罰之樞矣蕞爾島夷庸
===
不可滅之而朝食邪請以是而裨東南治
倭之略夫古今用兵不無勝敗勝敗分而
功罪彰矣是故懸之賞罰所以定功罪之
律而激厲其赴敵之心也然賞必當功而
無功者不濫與罰必當罪而有罪者不倖
避是兵之機宜也法之有常形而易見者
也乃若賞以酬功而微功或被殊恩罰以
懲罪而細罪顧罹顯戮身未冒乎矢石即
尺寸功未効也而優渥之典崇之跡方脫

translation_en: …and do not fear the enemy. I see commanders and soldiers united in purpose, their fighting spirit redoubled. Wherever I wish to employ them, they will go, even through water and fire. What enemy, then, could remain unsubdued, what stronghold unbreached, what violent disorder unsuppressed? Rewards and punishments are thus the practical means one uses to rouse men's hearts: the standard is established, and all can understand it. But to bend and stretch, to vary and transform, causing men to be turned about and stirred to action without their realizing it—this is extraordinary mastery in application, the subtle exercise of discretion by which enemies are subdued. Heroes and outstanding men employ it secretly without speaking of it, and others cannot fathom it. With those who understand this, one may discuss the variations of warfare; they know how to work the pivot of reward and punishment. Could we not destroy these paltry island barbarians before taking our morning meal? Allow me to use this principle to supplement the strategy for dealing with the Japanese raiders in the southeast. In warfare, past and present, there have inevitably been victories and defeats. Once victory and defeat are decided, merit and culpability become clear. Thus, publicly establishing rewards and punishments sets the rules for merit and culpability and spurs men to face the enemy. Yet rewards must correspond to merit, and those without merit must not receive them indiscriminately; punishments must correspond to offenses, and the guilty must not escape by good fortune. These are the practical principles of warfare, rules with a fixed form that is readily apparent. Yet there are cases in which rewards recompense merit, but a slight achievement may receive exceptional favor; punishments chastise offenses, but a minor offense may instead incur public execution. A man has not yet exposed himself to arrows and stones and has rendered not even the smallest service, yet lavish honors exalt him; another has only just withdrawn…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於鋒刃其勞勩宜卹也而斧鉞之誅不貸
卒至眇也一旦躋將帥之列將至尊也厥
苦樂與行伍均焉至有人不覬賞而倏忽
及之金帛炫燿三軍動色人不虞乎罰而
軍法加焉威如迅雷萬衆震慄是謂兵之
微權妙用之運也縱横開闔施之無定迹
而超於法之外者也是何也天下之心可
以術動千夫之勇可以氣激古之奇傑所
以禁暴誅亂而樹勛流聲者恒必繇之矣
===
野人盜食善馬獲之所必誅也秦穆顧賜
酒徧飲之然于韓之戰出公於淖中者竟
盜馬人也小卒自稱神師其謬妄可立照
也田單帥其衆拜禮之乃火牛之觸燕人
驚眩遂收恢齊之捷周泰身冒多矢孫權
撤所張蓋賜之厥後鼎足之業成泰之奮
勇多奇績焉此所謂用不測之恩而超格
以為賞故人莫不忘其生也苟晞為將姨
之子首犯軍律晞掩袂誅之不旋踵而奏

…from the blades of battle: his toil deserves compassionate consideration, yet execution by the headsman's axe is not remitted. A soldier occupies the humblest station, yet in a single day he is raised to the ranks of commanders; a commander holds the most exalted station, yet shares hardship and comfort equally with the rank and file. Some have no expectation of reward, yet it suddenly comes upon them: gold and silk gleam, and the whole army is visibly stirred. Others do not anticipate punishment, yet military law is brought to bear upon them: its might is like sudden thunder, and the assembled thousands tremble. This is what is meant by the exercise of subtle discretion and marvelous resourcefulness in warfare. Ranging freely, opening and closing, it follows no fixed pattern in its application and goes beyond established rules. Why is this? The hearts of all under Heaven can be moved by skillful means, and the courage of a thousand men can be roused by martial spirit. The extraordinary heroes of antiquity invariably relied on this to restrain violence, punish disorder, establish their achievements, and leave enduring renown.
Countrymen stole and ate a fine horse; once caught, they would surely have been executed. Yet Duke Mu of Qin instead bestowed wine and gave them all a drink. At the battle of Han, however, those who brought the duke out of the mire proved to be the very men who had stolen the horse. A common soldier proclaimed himself a divine master; the absurdity of his claim was immediately apparent. Yet Tian Dan led his men in bowing to him with due ceremony. Then, when the fire-bearing oxen charged, the men of Yan were terrified and bewildered, and he won the victory that restored Qi. Zhou Tai exposed himself to many arrows, and Sun Quan took down the canopy erected over himself and bestowed it upon him. Later, when the enterprise of establishing one of the three rival powers was accomplished, Tai's courageous exertions had yielded many remarkable achievements. This is what is meant by employing unexpected favor and going beyond the prescribed standards in granting rewards; thus everyone forgets concern for his own life. When Gou Xi was a commander, his maternal aunt's son was the first to violate military regulations. Xi covered his face with his sleeve and had him executed. Scarcely had he turned on his heel before he reported…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
卻敵之捷馬謖荆襄名士也街亭之戰違
授方略孔明揮涕收斬之不宥然祁山之
營仲達竟不敢越焉卒有折民匕筯高崇
文立命誅之未幾而檻闢平蜀弼成元和
之中興此用不測之威而超格以為罰故
人莫不忘其死也夫任俠之徒受人千金
之恩則以身許之而不悔寧有士被非常
之賞不愛主将如父母而忘生乎猛虎躡
其後懦夫越澗谷避之寧有士懽非常之
===
罰不畏主将如神明而忘死乎夫兵無甞
試固不宜膠成法以用於今然古人超格
之賞罰變通以盡神推行以盡妙無不可
也今之用兵而制敵者其果能達所要眇
指否邪欽惟
皇上至仁茂德綏懷遐邇薄海內外濡恩含澤
靡敢干紀久矣乃今蠢兹倭奴弄兵潢池
深入內訌禍延吳浙
聖天子睠念東南廣采臣工獻議行之如流精

…a victory in repelling the enemy. Ma Su was a celebrated gentleman of Jingzhou and Xiangyang. At the battle of Jieting, he disregarded the strategy he had been given. Kongming shed tears but had him arrested and beheaded, granting no pardon. Yet Zhongda ultimately did not dare advance beyond the encampment at Qishan. When a soldier broke a commoner's spoon and chopsticks, Gao Chongwen immediately ordered his execution. Soon afterward, the cages were opened [?] and Shu was pacified, helping bring about the restoration of the Yuanhe reign. This was to employ unfathomable severity and impose punishments beyond the ordinary rules; hence everyone disregarded the prospect of death. Men of chivalrous spirit, upon receiving the favor of a thousand pieces of gold, pledge their lives to their benefactor without regret. Could any soldier receive an extraordinary reward and fail to love his commander as his parents, forgetting concern for his own life? With a fierce tiger at his heels, even a coward will leap across ravines to escape. Could any soldier facing extraordinary punishment [?] fail to fear his commander as a divine power and disregard death? Warfare allows no trial runs, so one certainly should not cling rigidly to established methods in applying them today. Yet the ancients' rewards and punishments beyond the ordinary rules may all be used, adapting them to bring their efficacy fully into play and implementing them with consummate subtlety. Can those who now deploy troops and overcome the enemy truly grasp their subtle purport?
We reverently consider that His Majesty, in his utmost benevolence and abundant virtue, has brought peace and allegiance to those far and near. Throughout the realm and beyond, all have been steeped in his favor and bounty, and for a long time none has dared transgress the established order. But now these miscreant Japanese have stirred into action, brandishing weapons like rebels in a shallow pool, penetrating deep into the country and fomenting disorder within it, their devastation spreading through Wu and Zhejiang. The sagely Son of Heaven, solicitous for the southeast, has widely gathered proposals from his officials and put them into effect as readily as flowing water, carefully…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
擇將材博萃兵力日夕孜孜焉勦平之圖
治倭諸臣是宜恊忠宣力殄茲蕞孽以紓
當宁之懷以濟羣生之憤也乃勞師殫財淹玩
時月不聞汛掃鯨波以慰天下之望何邪
無亦當事者昧於通方之見牽於拘攣之
說逡廻顧忌苟覬目前不師古人非常之
賞罰以激厲闘士之心乎愚聞倭賊之來
歘如飄風至有變服操刅於左右而我兵
猶不覺者是何也哨探之無其人也夫哨
===
探之人當事者非不遣也然不立非常之
賞罰則人雖遣而未必行雖行而未必遠
其所以報覆乎我者非得諸途人之口則
其所造詐之辭也如是而欲知其聲息之
真可得乎古之名將於敵人屯營之所必
知其地之土石草木哨探之人責令取其
地產以爲左驗不然則立誅其妄矣於是
而倣行之不可以懾哨探者之心邪倭奴
之奸細布滿我地凡我兵之動息情狀彼

愚聞倭賊之來，歘如飄風，至有變服操刅於左右而我兵猶不覺者，是何也？哨探之無其人也。夫哨探之人，當事者非不遣也。然不立非常之賞罰，則人雖遣而未必行，雖行而未必遠。其所以報覆乎我者，非得諸途人之口，則其所造詐之辭也。如是而欲知其聲息之真，可得乎？古之名將，於敵人屯營之所，必知其地之土石草木。哨探之人，責令取其地產以爲左驗，不然則立誅其妄矣。於是而倣行之，不可以懾哨探者之心邪？倭奴之奸細布滿我地，凡我兵之動息情狀，彼
translation_en:
…selecting able commanders and broadly assembling military strength, striving diligently day and night to devise their suppression and pacification. The ministers charged with dealing with the Japanese pirates should unite in loyalty and exert their strength to annihilate these petty evildoers, thereby easing the sovereign’s anxiety and assuaging the people’s indignation. Yet they exhaust the troops and deplete resources, lingering and temporizing month after month; we hear of no sweeping clearance of the whale-tossed waves—the maritime raiders—to fulfill the hopes of all under Heaven. Why is this? Might those responsible lack a comprehensive understanding of how to adapt to circumstances, be constrained by rigid doctrines, hesitate and harbor misgivings, and seek only immediate advantage, failing to emulate the extraordinary rewards and punishments of the ancients to rouse the fighting men’s spirit?

I have heard that the Japanese pirates arrive as suddenly as a whirlwind. Some even change their clothing and wield blades beside our soldiers while our soldiers remain unaware. Why is this? Because suitable men are lacking among the scouts. It is not that those responsible do not dispatch scouts. But unless extraordinary rewards and punishments are established, men may be dispatched yet never go; even if they go, they may not venture far. What they report back to us is either something heard from travelers on the road or falsehoods of their own invention. Under such circumstances, can we obtain reliable intelligence about the enemy’s movements? The famous generals of antiquity invariably knew the soil, rocks, plants, and trees of the places where the enemy encamped. They required scouts to bring back things produced there as corroborating evidence; otherwise, they immediately executed them for false reporting. If we followed this practice here, could we not instill fear in the scouts’ hearts? The spies of those Japanese knaves are spread throughout our territory. As for every movement, halt, and circumstance of our troops, they…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
罔不諦知之而彼之虛實我兵無一人得
其纖毫者是何也死士之不募間諜之無
人也即有其人徒遙為探聽觀望之計以
塞責竟不知賊營所在也愚以為懸格外
之賞以募敢死之士與之約曰汝入賊中
幸生還則汝之富貴可立致儻不幸陷死
賊手則汝之父母妻屬破格尊養之子孫
世官流光無窮苟蓄異志必併汝父母妻
子戮之矣如是而賊之虛實不可得乎賊
===
之誘我也往往先歸我婦人令言賊中憂
怖狀及其来也多持金銀寶貝未合而佯
北即盡委金寶于路我兵不悟其狡相與
争拾取之彼之伏兵四起我師悉授首矣
使主将洞燭賊情明著賞罰之典令士卒
取賊委金若干即行斬首徇眾其不取金
者籍其名而厚賞之則賊不復以此計誘
我矣如是而賊之狡不可以漸阻邪其他
設竒以制變張疑以誘賊乘惰以砟營用

translation_en:
…they know every detail, yet not one of our soldiers can discover the slightest thing about their strengths and weaknesses. Why is this? Because men willing to die have not been recruited, and there is no one to serve as a spy. Even when such men are available, they merely listen for news and observe from afar to discharge their responsibilities; in the end, they do not even know where the enemy camp lies. In my humble opinion, extraordinary rewards should be offered to recruit men who dare to die, and an agreement made with them: “You are to enter the enemy’s midst. If you are fortunate enough to return alive, wealth and rank can be yours at once. If, unfortunately, you fall into enemy hands and die, your parents, wife, and dependants will be supported with exceptional honor, and your descendants will hold hereditary office, transmitting your glory without end. But if you harbor disloyal intentions, you will be executed together with your parents, wife, and children.” By these means, could we not discover the enemy’s strengths and weaknesses?

To lure us, the enemy often first sends back our women, instructing them to describe anxiety and fear among the enemy. When the enemy approaches, they carry much gold, silver, and other valuables. Before engaging, they feign flight and abandon all their treasure along the road. Our soldiers fail to recognize the trick and compete to pick it up. The enemy’s ambushed troops then rise on every side, and our entire force is put to the sword. If the commanding general thoroughly understood the enemy’s circumstances and clearly proclaimed the rules of reward and punishment, ordering that soldiers who took any of the gold abandoned by the enemy be immediately beheaded as a warning to the troops, while recording the names of those who took none and rewarding them generously, the enemy would no longer lure us with this scheme. Could not their cunning thus be gradually thwarted? As for other measures—devising surprise tactics to cope with changing circumstances, creating deceptive appearances to lure the enemy, taking advantage of their laxity to attack their camp [?], employing…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
間以携其黨潜火以焚其積百出雜出以
撓其謀靡不超格而賞罰之夫進有殊賞
以得其死力退有嚴刑以制其死命士孰
不捐軀以赴敵哉是故鋒鏑交於前而目
不眩矢石集于額而兵不却可殺可死可
陷可磔而不可使之敗矣神矣哉賞罰之
妙用乎然非其人不行也范蠡有言定傾
者與人而司馬相如則曰世必有非常之
人然後有非常之功夫非常者固常之所
異也昔之神聖人今雖未易及而
國初若徐常劉李諸賢亦不可復作已然英
傑彙征陳列中外豈無一二輩可紹先人
休烈邪近世若韓公雍之克大藤峽馬公
文升之勦黑水口余公子俊之襲虜榆林
王公守仁之平賊姚源皆能超格以行賞
罰而機宜妙用時出不窮故迄今尚嘉賴
其功不廢要眇之術神而明之存乎其人
古今未之易也芹曝之私愚生慨於中久

punctuated: 間以携其黨，潜火以焚其積，百出雜出以撓其謀，靡不超格而賞罰之。夫進有殊賞以得其死力，退有嚴刑以制其死命，士孰不捐軀以赴敵哉？是故鋒鏑交於前而目不眩，矢石集于額而兵不却，可殺可死可陷可磔，而不可使之敗矣。神矣哉，賞罰之妙用乎！然非其人不行也。范蠡有言：「定傾者與人。」而司馬相如則曰：「世必有非常之人，然後有非常之功。」夫非常者，固常之所異也。昔之神聖人，今雖未易及，而國初若徐常劉李諸賢，亦不可復作已。然英傑彙征，陳列中外，豈無一二輩可紹先人休烈邪？近世若韓公雍之克大藤峽，馬公文升之勦黑水口，余公子俊之襲虜榆林，王公守仁之平賊姚源，皆能超格以行賞罰，而機宜妙用，時出不窮，故迄今尚嘉賴其功不廢。要眇之術，神而明之，存乎其人，古今未之易也。芹曝之私，愚生慨於中久
translation_en: …use spies to divide their following, secretly set fires to burn their stores, and employ a hundred varied devices to disrupt their plans, in every case dispensing rewards and punishments beyond the ordinary rules. When advancing brings exceptional rewards that secure their utmost exertions unto death, and retreat brings severe penalties that hold their very lives in check, what soldier would not sacrifice himself to face the enemy? Thus, though blades and arrowheads clash before them, their eyes do not waver; though arrows and stones strike their foreheads, the troops do not retreat. They may be killed, may die, may be overwhelmed, may be dismembered, but they cannot be made to suffer defeat. How marvelous is the subtle application of rewards and punishments! Yet without the right person, it cannot be put into effect. Fan Li said, “Restoring stability when collapse threatens depends on men.” And Sima Xiangru said, “There must first be extraordinary men in the world before there can be extraordinary achievements.” What is extraordinary is indeed different from the ordinary. Though the divine sages of antiquity cannot readily be equaled today, even such worthies of our dynasty’s founding as Xu, Chang, Liu, and Li cannot be brought back to life. Yet outstanding men have come forward together and hold posts at court and in the provinces. Could there not be one or two among them capable of carrying on their predecessors’ glorious achievements? In recent times, Lord Han Yong’s conquest of Dateng Gorge, Lord Ma Wensheng’s suppression of the enemy at Heishuikou, Lord Yu Zijun’s surprise attack on the northern foes at Yulin, and Lord Wang Shouren’s pacification of the rebels at Yaoyuan all exemplified the ability to go beyond ordinary rules in administering rewards and punishments. Their subtle application of measures suited to the occasion continually produced fresh responses without end. Thus, even now, their achievements remain esteemed and continue to benefit us. As for these profound and subtle arts, their inspired and discerning application rests with the person: this has never changed, from antiquity to the present. In the humble spirit of one offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I, an unworthy scholar, have long felt deeply stirred within…

矣敢攄發以復幸勿嗤爲空談幸甚
第五問
潘文端
同考試官教諭徐批詭行畸節其孤介
若足以矯俗然不免爲中道所擯是作指數于瑕瑜
而律以聖人之行其知定人物之衡者乎
考試官侍講袁批以中行繩獨行見道之
士也
考試官右諭德王批節士本不可少但不可
===
爲訓耳此策得之
聖人之視天下猶一家也其視天下之人
猶一身也故世有紛難必思批之世有劻
勷必思定之猶之有家者顧家有身者顧
身也今夫天乆雨墻垣圯以爲不嚴且有
盜汲汲然不俟明日而連築者顧家也病
五日不起未甚也客有言秦越人者知禁
方能已人之疾則裹金馳使而請之顧身
也世有紛難劻勷之事而掉臂不顧高枕

猶一身也故世有紛難必思拯之世有勛
勸必思定之猶之有家者顧家有身者顧

也世有紛難勛勸之事而掉臂不顧高枕
punctuated:
矣，敢攄發以復，幸勿嗤爲空談，幸甚。

第五問
潘文端

同考試官教諭徐批：「詭行畸節，其孤介若足以矯俗，然不免爲中道所擯。是作指數于瑕瑜，而律以聖人之行，其知定人物之衡者乎？」

考試官侍講袁批：「以中行繩獨行，見道之士也。」

考試官右諭德王批：「節士本不可少，但不可爲訓耳。此策得之。」

聖人之視天下，猶一家也；其視天下之人，猶一身也。故世有紛難，必思批之；世有劻勷，必思定之。猶之有家者顧家，有身者顧身也。今夫天乆雨，墻垣圯，以爲不嚴且有盜，汲汲然不俟明日而連築者，顧家也。病五日不起，未甚也，客有言秦越人者，知禁方，能已人之疾，則裹金馳使而請之，顧身也。世有紛難劻勷之事，而掉臂不顧，高枕
translation_en:
…I venture to express these thoughts in reply. I would be most grateful if you did not deride them as empty talk.

Fifth Question
Pan Wenduan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Unconventional conduct and eccentric integrity, in their aloof steadfastness, may seem sufficient to correct prevailing customs, yet they inevitably fall short of the middle way. This essay enumerates their flaws and merits [?] and measures them against the conduct of the sage. Does its author not understand how to establish the scales for judging people?”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Expositor: “He measures solitary conduct by the standard of the middle way: a scholar who perceives the Way.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Right Mentor: “Men of unbending integrity are certainly indispensable; it is simply that their conduct cannot serve as a general rule. This policy essay grasps that point.”

The sage regards all under Heaven as a single household, and its people as a single body. Thus, whenever the world suffers tangled difficulties, he invariably seeks to resolve them; whenever it suffers turmoil, he invariably seeks to settle it. He is like someone who has a household and cares for it, or someone who has a body and cares for it. Suppose prolonged rain causes the enclosing walls to collapse. Believing that the house is insecure and that thieves may come, its owner urgently sets about rebuilding them, without waiting until the next day: this is caring for one’s household. Suppose someone has been ill and unable to rise for five days, though the illness is not yet severe. A visitor mentions a man named Qin Yueren, who knows secret remedies and can cure people’s illnesses. The patient then wraps up some gold and dispatches a messenger at speed to invite him: this is caring for one’s body. Yet when tangled difficulties and turmoil arise in the world, someone may swing his arms unconcernedly, pay no heed, and rest his head high upon his pillow…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不来是視天下不如家視天下之人不如
身也聖人弗爲也是故駕敝車策羸駟軋
軋以行于四方而弗以爲憊也干七十二
國而弗遇乃猶使子貢之徒摇唇鼓舌游
揚于諸侯之間偲偲然兾萬一之聽而弗
以爲倦也上嘉唐虞下樂二周如有用我
者執此以往而弗以爲夸也及得定公而
相焉則即墮三都去正卯而弗以爲横也
既用弗卒則即退栖于杏壇之上與七十
===
子之徒講道而論治焉以立百王之準而
弗以爲髙也用則往不用則引而退又復
用又復往又復不用又復引而退聖人不
厭其煩者凡以爲天下也思欲批紛難定
劻勷伸唐虞之志而樂行二周之道也方
今海内爲一既異于春秋之世而
聖明在御天下抱竒之士畢集于廷林藪窟宅
皆虚而無人何者用之也令孔子而生當
斯世則亦且車馬不疲杏壇無講矣何者

既用弗卒則即退栖于杏壇之上與七十
===

弗以爲高也用則往不用則引而退又復
用又復往又復不用又復引而退聖人不
厭其煩者凡以爲天下也思欲批紛難定
勔勤伸唐虞之志而樂行二周之道也方
今海内爲一既異于春秋之世而
聖明在御天下抱奇之士畢集于廷林藪窟宅
皆虚而無人何者用之也令孔子而生當
斯世則亦且車馬不疲杏壇無講矣何者
punctuated:
不来，是視天下不如家，視天下之人不如身也，聖人弗爲也。是故駕敝車，策羸駟，軋軋以行于四方，而弗以爲憊也。干七十二國而弗遇，乃猶使子貢之徒摇唇鼓舌，游揚于諸侯之間，偲偲然兾萬一之聽，而弗以爲倦也。上嘉唐虞，下樂二周，「如有用我者」，執此以往，而弗以爲夸也。及得定公而相焉，則即墮三都，去正卯，而弗以爲横也。既用弗卒，則即退栖于杏壇之上，與七十子之徒講道而論治焉，以立百王之準，而弗以爲髙也。用則往，不用則引而退；又復用，又復往；又復不用，又復引而退。聖人不厭其煩者，凡以爲天下也，思欲批紛難，定劻勷，伸唐虞之志，而樂行二周之道也。
方今海内爲一，既異于春秋之世，而聖明在御，天下抱竒之士畢集于廷，林藪窟宅皆虚而無人。何者？用之也。令孔子而生當斯世，則亦且車馬不疲，杏壇無講矣。何者？
translation_en:
…and does not come [?], this is to regard the realm as less important than one’s household, and its people as less important than one’s own body. The sage would not act thus. Hence he rode in a battered carriage, urged on a team of four emaciated horses, and went creaking through the four quarters, without considering it exhausting. He sought employment in seventy-two states but found no receptive ruler. Still he sent Zigong and his other disciples to plead his case and commend him among the feudal lords, earnestly hoping that someone might listen, however slight the chance, and never considered it wearisome. Looking to the distant past, he esteemed Tang and Yu; looking to more recent times, he delighted in the two Zhou dynasties. “If someone would employ me,” he said: holding fast to these ideals, he went forward without considering his aspirations extravagant. When he gained the support of Duke Ding and served as his minister, he promptly demolished the fortifications of the three cities and removed Zheng Mao 正卯 [?], without considering his actions high-handed. When his employment failed to continue to its conclusion, he withdrew to dwell at the Apricot Altar, where he expounded the Way and discussed government with his seventy disciples, establishing a standard for a hundred generations of kings without considering it too lofty. When employed, he went forward; when not employed, he withdrew. Employed again, he again went forward; once more denied employment, he again withdrew. That the sage never tired of this trouble was entirely for the sake of the realm. He wished to untangle its difficulties, settle its turmoil, fulfill the aspirations of Tang and Yu, and joyfully put into practice the Way of the two Zhou dynasties.
Now all within the seas is united, a situation already different from that of the Spring and Autumn period. With our sagacious sovereign upon the throne, men of exceptional talent from throughout the realm have all assembled at court. The forests, marshes, and secluded dwellings are empty, with no one remaining there. Why? Because these men are employed. Were Confucius to be born into this age, neither his carriage nor his horses would be worn out, and there would be no teaching at the Apricot Altar. Why? …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
遇之也而世之君子顧乃有稱鮑焦爰旌
目荆輿顏闔段干木魯仲連之倫者以爲
此六子者皆能遁世好隱不沒于利不牽
于勢此高節之士獨行之賢也欣慕之焉
嗟乎此猶之厭粱肉而思藜莧謝淄澠之
水而甘行潦也悖之甚矣夫學也者學爲
聖人耳聖人出處進退之跡固在也所謂
無意無必無固無我者也而今之君子離
聖而語行違道而談節出者皆卑則律以
===
六子處者皆高則附于六子若而人者即
非幻民亦屬狂子愚不得不辯故愚嘗謂
隱有四術而君子察焉有炯然抱奇而固
請不見其名曰石隱欲觀我奇而令我見
才一見之而輒復收之其名曰高隱度無
所見而託號以覆短其名曰智隱空自以
身爲枯木朽株而尺寸無聞其名曰痴隱
此四術者君子不可弗察也夫所謂石隱
者則段干木其人是已所謂高隱者則魯

punctuated:
遇之也。而世之君子顧乃有稱鮑焦、爰旌目、荆輿、顏闔、段干木、魯仲連之倫者，以爲此六子者皆能遁世好隱，不沒于利，不牽于勢，此高節之士、獨行之賢也，欣慕之焉。嗟乎！此猶之厭粱肉而思藜莧，謝淄澠之水而甘行潦也，悖之甚矣！夫學也者，學爲聖人耳。聖人出處進退之跡固在也，所謂無意、無必、無固、無我者也。而今之君子離聖而語行，違道而談節，出者皆卑，則律以六子；處者皆高，則附于六子。若而人者，即非幻民，亦屬狂子，愚不得不辯。
故愚嘗謂隱有四術，而君子察焉。有炯然抱奇而固請不見，其名曰石隱；欲觀我奇而令我見，才一見之而輒復收之，其名曰高隱；度無所見而託號以覆短，其名曰智隱；空自以身爲枯木朽株，而尺寸無聞，其名曰痴隱。此四術者，君子不可弗察也。夫所謂石隱者，則段干木其人是已；所謂高隱者，則魯
translation_en:
…because he would have met with appreciative recognition. Yet among the gentlemen of our age there are those who praise such men as Bao Jiao, Yuan Jingmu, Jing Yu, Yan He, Duangan Mu, and Lu Zhonglian. They believe that these six all managed to withdraw from the world and delight in seclusion, neither submerged in profit nor drawn by power. They admire and long to emulate them as men of lofty integrity and worthies of independent conduct. Alas! This is like tiring of fine grain and meat and craving goosefoot and amaranth, or rejecting the waters of the Zi and Mian rivers and relishing roadside puddles. How utterly perverse! Learning means simply learning to become a sage. The precedents of the sages’ taking office or remaining in retirement, advancing or withdrawing, are plainly there: what is meant by having no arbitrary preconceptions, no insistence on certainty, no obstinacy, and no self-centeredness. Yet today’s gentlemen discuss conduct apart from the sages and integrity in defiance of the Way. They consider all who take office base, measuring them against these six; they consider all who remain in retirement lofty, ranking them alongside these six. Such people, even if they are not deceivers, are certainly wild eccentrics. I cannot but dispute their views.
Thus I have often said that there are four methods of reclusion, which gentlemen should scrutinize. One possesses conspicuous, exceptional abilities yet firmly insists on not appearing: this is called “stone reclusion.” Another thinks, “You wish to behold my exceptional qualities and have me appear”; he reveals them only once, then immediately conceals them again: this is called “lofty reclusion.” Another judges that he has nothing to display and adopts the reputation of a recluse to conceal his shortcomings: this is called “clever reclusion.” Another merely makes himself into a withered tree or rotten stump, without the slightest achievement becoming known: this is called “foolish reclusion.” Gentlemen must scrutinize these four methods. As for what is called “stone reclusion,” Duangan Mu is precisely such a man; as for what is called “lofty reclusion,” Lu…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
仲連其人是已所謂智隱者則荆與顏闔
其人是已所謂痴隱者則鮑焦爰旌目其
人是已夫鮑焦者吾不知其何許人也第
聞其衣敝衣持蔬而遇子貢于道也子貢
曰吁吾子苦矣衣敝而蔬之持也鮑焦以
言摧子貢子貢亦以言摧鮑焦焦愧而立
槁于洛水之上焉爰旌目者東方之士也
餓于道有狐父之盜曰丘者見而下壺餐
以餔之已而知其爲狐父之盜也乃吐之
===
而兩手據地喀喀而不出竟伏地而不起
也夫此二子者皆古之所謂高節獨行之
士也亦徒聞其能不辱耳而史不著其他
奇貨可張設施行也夫其不辱也固昔人
之所謂枯木朽株耳不亦愚乎若彼鮑子
憤世不用蓋與世猶未絕也乃不能忍痛
須時而輕投其身于空虚無用之地此侍
人婢子之所爲一不得意輒効于榻前以
爲無復之耳昔卞生三刖其足矣乃懷璞

punctuated:
仲連其人是已。所謂智隱者，則荆與、顏闔其人是已。所謂痴隱者，則鮑焦、爰旌目其人是已。
夫鮑焦者，吾不知其何許人也，第聞其衣敝衣、持蔬而遇子貢于道也。子貢曰：「吁！吾子苦矣，衣敝而蔬之持也。」鮑焦以言摧子貢，子貢亦以言摧鮑焦。焦愧而立槁于洛水之上焉。爰旌目者，東方之士也，餓于道。有狐父之盜曰丘者，見而下壺餐以餔之。已而知其爲狐父之盜也，乃吐之，而兩手據地，喀喀而不出，竟伏地而不起也。
夫此二子者，皆古之所謂高節獨行之士也，亦徒聞其能不辱耳，而史不著其他奇貨可張設施行也。夫其不辱也，固昔人之所謂枯木朽株耳，不亦愚乎？若彼鮑子，憤世不用，蓋與世猶未絕也，乃不能忍痛須時，而輕投其身于空虚無用之地。此侍人婢子之所爲，一不得意，輒効于榻前，以爲無復之耳。昔卞生三刖其足矣，乃懷璞
translation_en:
…Zhonglian is just such a man. Those exemplifying so-called calculating reclusion are Jing Yu [?] and Yan He. Those exemplifying so-called foolish reclusion are Bao Jiao and Yuan Jingmu.
As for Bao Jiao, I do not know where he came from. I have only heard that, wearing tattered clothes and carrying vegetables, he encountered Zigong on the road. Zigong said, “Ah! How you suffer, sir, dressed in rags and carrying vegetables!” Bao Jiao assailed Zigong with words, and Zigong likewise assailed Bao Jiao with words. Ashamed, Bao Jiao stood on the bank of the Luo River and withered away. Yuan Jingmu was a man of the eastern region. He was starving by the roadside when a robber from Hufu named Qiu saw him, set down a vessel of food, and fed him. Later, learning that the man was a robber from Hufu, he tried to vomit it up. Bracing both hands against the ground, he retched repeatedly but could bring nothing up. In the end, he fell prostrate and never rose again.
These two men were both what the ancients called men of lofty integrity and independent conduct. Yet we hear only that they could keep themselves free from disgrace; the histories record no other exceptional gifts of theirs that could be displayed or put into practice [?]. Their freedom from disgrace was, after all, merely what earlier men called being withered trees and rotten stumps. Was this not foolish? Take Master Bao: he resented the world for not employing him, which suggests that he had not yet severed his ties with it. Yet he could not endure his pain and await the right time, and instead lightly cast himself into emptiness and uselessness. This is how attendants and maidservants behave: at the slightest disappointment, they immediately do the same before the couch, thinking thereby to put an end to everything [?]. In former times, Master Bian suffered the amputation of his feet three times [?], yet still clasped his uncut jade…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
呱呱而不去彼亦謂須識者耳卞生不肯
亡璞竟剖見珍且乃獲賞鮑子不聞斯道
而徒以憤斃故曰痴隱聖人所不道君子
所不由也荆輿者荆人也楚王使使者齎
百金造門曰請先生治河南荆輿不許也
遂負釜戴絰而與其妻去莫知所之顔闔
者魯人也魯君將造闔使人以幣先焉使
者及門而見闔闔紿使者去使者復来闔
鑿坯而遁矣夫君子之所爲重進者蓋謂
===
其無禮耳今楚既齎金魯亦攝幣可謂有
禮矣乃荆輿滅影顔闔竄跡此之不往則
又何須也昔宋人有寶燕石以爲王者襲
以十巾藏以革匱人不得觀焉既發藏則
乃燕石也觀者俛首掩口而笑焉則此二
子者乃亦寶燕石而懼其發藏以賈笑也
乃固祕之耳嗟乎兎絲燕麥徒有其名踽
鼎烹雞豈其任乎故引而逃去而且博捐
金輕幣之譽以遺後世又有高節獨行之

乃固祕之耳嗟乎兎絲燕麥徒有其名蹻
鼎烹雞豈其任乎故引而逃去而且慱捐
金輕幣之譽以遺後世又有高節獨行之
punctuated:
呱呱而不去，彼亦謂須識者耳。卞生不肯亡璞，竟剖見珍，且乃獲賞。鮑子不聞斯道，而徒以憤斃，故曰痴隱，聖人所不道，君子所不由也。
荆輿者，荆人也。楚王使使者齎百金造門，曰：「請先生治河南。」荆輿不許也，遂負釜戴絰，而與其妻去，莫知所之。顔闔者，魯人也。魯君將造闔，使人以幣先焉。使者及門而見闔，闔紿使者去。使者復来，闔鑿坯而遁矣。夫君子之所爲重進者，蓋謂其無禮耳。今楚既齎金，魯亦攝幣，可謂有禮矣。乃荆輿滅影，顔闔竄跡，此之不往，則又何須也？昔宋人有寶燕石以爲王者，襲以十巾，藏以革匱，人不得觀焉。既發藏，則乃燕石也。觀者俛首掩口而笑焉。則此二子者，乃亦寶燕石，而懼其發藏以賈笑也，乃固祕之耳。嗟乎！兎絲燕麥，徒有其名；踽鼎烹雞，豈其任乎？故引而逃去，而且博捐金輕幣之譽，以遺後世，又有高節獨行之
translation_en:
…weeping aloud yet refusing to leave: he too meant only to await someone who could recognize its worth. Master Bian would not abandon his unworked jade; eventually it was cut open and its precious contents revealed, and he was rewarded as well. Master Bao had not learned this principle and merely died in indignation. Thus this is called foolish reclusion: something the sage does not commend and the gentleman does not practice.
Jing Yu was a man of Jing. The king of Chu sent a messenger to his door bearing a hundred measures of gold, saying, “We ask you, sir, to govern Henan.” Jing Yu refused. Carrying a cooking pot on his back and wearing a mourning headband, he departed with his wife, and no one knew where he went. Yan He was a man of Lu. The ruler of Lu intended to visit him and sent someone ahead with gifts of silk. The messenger reached his door and met him, but Yan He tricked the messenger into leaving. When the messenger returned, Yan He had broken through his earthen wall and fled.
The reason a gentleman is cautious about entering service is surely that the invitation lacks proper courtesy. Yet Chu had brought gold, and Lu too had provided silk: these invitations could be called courteous. Nevertheless, Jing Yu vanished from sight and Yan He concealed his tracks. If they would not respond to such invitations, what more were they waiting for? Once there was a man of Song who treasured a stone from Yan, taking it for jade [?]. He wrapped it in ten cloths and stored it in a leather chest, allowing no one to see it. When he opened his hoard, however, it proved to be merely a stone from Yan. Those who saw it lowered their heads, covered their mouths, and laughed. These two men likewise treasured mere stones from Yan, fearing that opening their hoards would invite ridicule; that was all they were so determined to keep secret.
Alas! Dodder and wild oats possess only the names of silk and grain. Could a cauldron for cooking a chicken [?] be equal to the task? Thus they withdrew and fled, while also winning a reputation for rejecting gold and disdaining silk to be passed down to posterity, and acquiring the air of lofty integrity and independent conduct…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
風故曰智隱聖人所不道君子所不由也
夫既聖人不肯道君子不可由矣而後世
轉稱之何也以其賢于貪生而優于競進
也於戲吾竊痛後世之爲士者焉較利害
于毫毛之微而爭功名于尺寸之間託名
千金坐不垂堂何其怯也已觸三面乞以
一目見脫何其哀也積澤之火不捄而麗
水之金顧採何其智也食嗟來之食何其
苟也伏在車下泣血孫陽何其卑也突梯
===
滑稽以叨升斗何其汙也貶抑孟陬自前
進御何其妬也日置驛馬請謝賓客唯恐
不徧何其周也得近霸王不羞牛口又何
辱也四至九卿甘宦若飴又何巧也身處
江湖心懸魏闕又何鄙也懊不得意坐而
書空又何隘也若此類者不能舍生不能
遺榮令與立枯吐哺之輩負甕鑿坯之倫
同日而並論則高下相絶奚啻萬里無恠
乎後世之有述也然以聖人處之則不若

punctuated: 風。故曰：「智隱，聖人所不道，君子所不由也。」夫既聖人不肯道，君子不可由矣，而後世轉稱之，何也？以其賢于貪生而優于競進也。於戲！吾竊痛後世之爲士者焉！較利害于毫毛之微，而爭功名于尺寸之間；託名千金，坐不垂堂，何其怯也！已觸三面，乞以一目見脫，何其哀也！積澤之火不捄，而麗水之金顧採，何其智也！食嗟來之食，何其苟也！伏在車下，泣血孫陽，何其卑也！突梯滑稽，以叨升斗，何其汙也！貶抑孟陬，自前進御，何其妬也！日置驛馬，請謝賓客，唯恐不徧，何其周也！得近霸王，不羞牛口，又何辱也！四至九卿，甘宦若飴，又何巧也！身處江湖，心懸魏闕，又何鄙也！懊不得意，坐而書空，又何隘也！若此類者，不能舍生，不能遺榮，令與立枯吐哺之輩、負甕鑿坯之倫，同日而並論，則高下相絶，奚啻萬里！無恠乎後世之有述也！然以聖人處之，則不若
translation_en:
…the bearing of men of lofty integrity and independent conduct. Thus it is said: “Calculated reclusion is something the sage does not commend and the gentleman does not practice.” Since the sage will not commend it and the gentleman must not practice it, why have later generations nevertheless praised it? Because it is worthier than clinging to life and better than competing for advancement.
Alas! I privately grieve over the scholars of later ages! They weigh advantage and harm down to a hair’s breadth and contend for merit and fame inch by inch. Invoking the saying that a man worth a thousand pieces of gold does not sit beneath the eaves, how cowardly they are! Already caught in a net on three sides, they beg to escape through a single mesh—how pitiable! They leave the fire at Jize [?] unquenched, yet turn to gathering gold from the Li River—how calculating! They eat food offered with a contemptuous summons—how heedless of principle! Crouching beneath a carriage, they weep tears of blood before Sun Yang—how abject! Slippery and glib, they cadge a few measures of grain—how sordid! They disparage Mengzou [?] and push themselves forward to enter the ruler’s service—how jealous! Daily they have post horses made ready to invite guests and pay their respects, fearing only that someone might be missed—how thorough! To gain access to a hegemonic ruler, they feel no shame at tending cattle—what humiliation! Four times they attain the rank of minister among the Nine Courts, savoring office like malt sugar—how cunning! Their bodies remain among the rivers and lakes, but their hearts hang upon the palace gates—how base! Chagrined at frustrated ambitions, they sit tracing characters in the air—how narrow-minded!
Such men cannot relinquish life or set aside glory. Were they compared on equal terms with those who withered away standing or spat out their food, those who carried water jars or broke through earthen walls to escape office, the distance between the high and the low would be far more than ten thousand li! No wonder later generations have celebrated those recluses! Yet if a sage were placed in their circumstances, he would not…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
是然耳自聖人而降則唯段干木魯仲連
之二子者其庶幾焉夫秦將將四十萬之
衆而東圍邯鄲也趙危若累棊存亡在俛
仰之頃矣趙且欲尊秦為帝以免難也仲
連固不肯而語中有竒殷殷乎有動衆傾
秦之術秦將聞之為引軍去趙得不亡者
仲連之力也趙欲封仲連仲連辭不受壽
之金亦辭遂去而逃之海上終身不見也
夫却秦存趙不亦偉乎避爵辭金不亦潔
===
乎故曰仲連高隱言善見又善藏也魏在
春秋為小國秦視滅魏若摶豚鼠耳然竟
文侯之身不敢加兵于魏者則段干木在
焉文侯嘗欲相干木矣干木不肯也乃日
造館而請事焉秦將攻魏諫者曰夫魏不
可攻也段干木賢者也而魏禮之尚可以
加兵乎秦遂輟兵不行夫不就祿位非潔
乎趺坐高談令所居之邦不危非才乎故
曰干木石隱言堅不可移也世之君子賢

乎趺坐高談令所居之邦不危非才乎故
曰干木石隱言堅不可移也世之君子賢
punctuated:
是然耳。自聖人而降，則唯段干木、魯仲連之二子者，其庶幾焉。夫秦將將四十萬之衆而東圍邯鄲也，趙危若累棊，存亡在俛仰之頃矣。趙且欲尊秦為帝以免難也，仲連固不肯，而語中有竒，殷殷乎有動衆傾秦之術。秦將聞之，為引軍去。趙得不亡者，仲連之力也。趙欲封仲連，仲連辭不受；壽之金，亦辭，遂去而逃之海上，終身不見也。夫却秦存趙，不亦偉乎？避爵辭金，不亦潔乎？故曰仲連高隱，言善見又善藏也。
魏在春秋為小國，秦視滅魏若摶豚鼠耳。然竟文侯之身，不敢加兵于魏者，則段干木在焉。文侯嘗欲相干木矣，干木不肯也，乃日造館而請事焉。秦將攻魏，諫者曰：「夫魏不可攻也。段干木賢者也，而魏禮之，尚可以加兵乎？」秦遂輟兵不行。夫不就祿位，非潔乎？趺坐高談，令所居之邦不危，非才乎？故曰干木石隱，言堅不可移也。世之君子賢
translation_en:
…merely so. Below the sages, only those two men, Duan Ganmu and Lu Zhonglian, came close to this ideal. When a Qin general led a force of four hundred thousand eastward to besiege Handan, Zhao was as precarious as a pile of gaming pieces; its survival or destruction hung upon an instant. Zhao was about to honor the ruler of Qin as emperor to escape disaster. Zhonglian firmly refused to countenance this. His words possessed an extraordinary power, resounding with the means to move the multitude and overthrow Qin. On hearing them, the Qin general withdrew his army. That Zhao escaped destruction was due to Zhonglian’s efforts. Zhao wished to grant Zhonglian a fief, but he declined it. He likewise refused the gold offered to honor him, then departed and withdrew to the seacoast, never appearing again for the rest of his life. Was not repelling Qin and preserving Zhao a magnificent achievement? Was not shunning rank and refusing gold a mark of integrity? Thus Zhonglian is called a lofty recluse: he knew both how to appear and how to conceal himself.
Wei was a small state in the Spring and Autumn period. Qin regarded destroying Wei as no harder than seizing a piglet or a rat. Yet throughout Marquis Wen’s lifetime, Qin dared not attack Wei, because Duan Ganmu was there. Marquis Wen once wished to appoint Ganmu as his chief minister, but Ganmu refused. The marquis therefore visited his dwelling daily and asked to serve him. When Qin was about to attack Wei, an adviser remonstrated: “Wei must not be attacked. Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with due ceremony. Can we still take up arms against it?” Qin consequently called off its military expedition. Was not refusing salaried office a mark of integrity? Was not sitting cross-legged and discoursing on lofty matters, while keeping the state in which he lived safe from danger, a mark of ability? Thus Ganmu is called a rock-like recluse: he was steadfast and could not be moved. The gentlemen of this world regard as worthy…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
干木而右仲連者獨稱其讓封避相以爲
高節獨行之士也而不知二子之所以爲
賢者不獨在讓封避相在却敵免難耳不
費一領甲不食一斗粟而置兩國于磐石
之上敵人虎視狼顧而莫敢誰何此其人
豈徒沁沁泯泯居無一物者邪故即不出
出即犖犖即不隱隱即冥冥譬之若神龍
然能潛能見能上能下不可以形跡拘不
可以網羅求也然此唯仲連能當之耳若
===
彼干木者塊處石室彈琴樂道以咏先王
之風而不顧人世有拯溺之事其於聖人
之出處何乎然能抑秦王之虎心不可及
也仲連一試而遁秦雖釋趙螫必中于他
若使仲連拜趙之封而以所壽之千金爲
資養賓客以親秦約與國而申誓歡樂則
相賀患難則相援亦庶幾哉與桓文之霸
業比隆矣而卒乃逃去爲德不博棄百代
之烈而薄收須臾之譽非聖人之槩也然

出即舉舉即不隱隱即莫莫譬之若神龍
然能潛能見能上能下不可以形跡拘不
可以網羅求也然此唯仲連能當之耳若
===
彼干木者塊處石室彈琴樂道以咏先王
之風而不顧人世有拯溺之事其於聖人
之出處何乎然能抑秦王之虎心不可及
也仲連一試而遁秦雖釋趙盤必中于他
若使仲連拜趙之封而以所壽之千金爲
資養賓客以親秦約與國而申誓歡樂則
相賀患難則相援亦庶幾哉與桓文之覇
業比隆矣而卒乃逃去爲德不博棄百代
之烈而薄收須史之譽非聖人之槩也然
punctuated: 干木而右仲連者，獨稱其讓封避相，以爲高節獨行之士也，而不知二子之所以爲賢者，不獨在讓封避相，在却敵免難耳。不費一領甲，不食一斗粟，而置兩國于磐石之上，敵人虎視狼顧，而莫敢誰何。此其人豈徒沁沁泯泯、居無一物者邪？故即不出，出即犖犖；即不隱，隱即冥冥。譬之若神龍然，能潛能見，能上能下，不可以形跡拘，不可以網羅求也。然此唯仲連能當之耳。若彼干木者，塊處石室，彈琴樂道，以咏先王之風，而不顧人世有拯溺之事，其於聖人之出處何乎？然能抑秦王之虎心，不可及也。仲連一試而遁，秦雖釋趙，螫必中于他。若使仲連拜趙之封，而以所壽之千金爲資，養賓客以親秦，約與國而申誓，歡樂則相賀，患難則相援，亦庶幾哉！與桓文之霸業比隆矣。而卒乃逃去，爲德不博，棄百代之烈，而薄收須臾之譽，非聖人之槩也。然
translation_en:
…those who esteem Ganmu and honor Zhonglian praise only their refusal of enfeoffment and avoidance of appointment as chief minister, considering them men of lofty integrity and independent conduct. They do not understand that what made these two men worthy lay not merely in refusing enfeoffment and avoiding ministerial office, but in repelling enemies and averting calamity. Without expending a single suit of armor or consuming a single peck of grain, they placed two states upon foundations as firm as rock. Their enemies watched like tigers and glanced about like wolves, yet none dared challenge them. Could such men merely have been obscure and withdrawn [?], dwelling in possession of nothing? Thus, if they did not come forward, they remained apart; once they came forward, they were outstanding. If they did not withdraw, they remained visible; once they withdrew, they vanished into obscurity. They were like divine dragons, able to submerge or appear, ascend or descend: they could not be confined by outward traces or sought with nets. Yet only Zhonglian truly merits this description.
As for Ganmu, he dwelt alone in a stone chamber, playing the zither and delighting in the Way, singing of the legacy of the former kings, while ignoring the work of rescuing the drowning in the human world. How does this accord with the sages’ principles of entering service and withdrawing? Yet his ability to restrain the King of Qin’s tiger-like heart was beyond others’ reach.
Zhonglian made one attempt and then fled. Although Qin released Zhao, its sting was sure to strike elsewhere. Had Zhonglian accepted Zhao’s enfeoffment and used the thousand pieces of gold offered him as a gift to support retainers and cultivate friendship with Qin, made covenants with allied states and renewed their oaths, so that they congratulated one another in times of joy and aided one another in adversity, he might indeed have approached the ideal! His achievement could have rivaled the hegemony of Dukes Huan and Wen. Yet in the end he fled, and the benefits of his virtue did not extend far. He abandoned an achievement that could have endured for a hundred generations, gathering instead a meager harvest of momentary praise. This was not the stature of a sage. Yet…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
能以三寸之舌折强秦四十萬之衆不可
及也由此觀之則論士者必投之猝至之
難以觀其才焉才既明矣又試之非意之
榮以觀其操焉操既得矣又納之死生之
地以觀其志焉才足以批難矣操足以遺
榮矣志足以忘軀矣備斯數道而甘就閒
寂終身枯槁乃稱曰高隱也三者缺一焉
猶屬之智隱也夫智隱非傑也痴隱非情
也石隱非道也高隱非聖也彼六子者皆
===
非也即有慕其聲而趨之者又以非蹈非
也於乎君臣之義其在天地之間也猶之
逃雨焉無之而非是履其土而欲潔其躬
非也竊其名而佯棄其名非也謂隱獨高
非也謂出獨卑非也謂世莫我知非之又
非者也夫人也以身盛心以心盛智一人
一心一心一智故一人不能當十人之視
而視者不止十人一心不能當十心之疑
而疑者不止十人彼六子者千百世以前

也石隱非道也高隱非聖也彼六子者皆
===

也於乎君臣之義其在天地之間也猶之

一心一心一智故一人不能當十人之視
而視者不止十人一心不能當十心之疑
而疑者不止十人彼六子者千百世以前
punctuated:
能以三寸之舌折强秦四十萬之衆，不可及也。由此觀之，則論士者必投之猝至之難，以觀其才焉；才既明矣，又試之非意之榮，以觀其操焉；操既得矣，又納之死生之地，以觀其志焉。才足以批難矣，操足以遺榮矣，志足以忘軀矣，備斯數道而甘就閒寂，終身枯槁，乃稱曰高隱也。三者缺一焉，猶屬之智隱也。夫智隱非傑也，痴隱非情也，石隱非道也，高隱非聖也。彼六子者，皆非也。即有慕其聲而趨之者，又以非蹈非也。
於乎！君臣之義，其在天地之間也，猶之逃雨焉，無之而非是。履其土而欲潔其躬，非也；竊其名而佯棄其名，非也；謂隱獨高，非也；謂出獨卑，非也；謂世莫我知，非之又非者也。夫人也，以身盛心，以心盛智，一人一心，一心一智。故一人不能當十人之視，而視者不止十人；一心不能當十心之疑，而疑者不止十人。彼六子者，千百世以前
translation_en:
…his ability, with his three-inch tongue, to repel mighty Qin’s force of four hundred thousand was beyond anyone’s match. Viewed in this light, anyone judging a scholar must cast him into a suddenly arising crisis to observe his ability. Once his ability is clear, he must then be tested with unexpected honors to observe his integrity. Once his integrity has been established, he must then be placed in a situation of life and death to observe his resolve. His ability must suffice to resolve difficulties, his integrity to forsake honors, and his resolve to disregard his own life. Only when he possesses all these qualities, yet willingly embraces quiet seclusion and spends his entire life in privation, may he be called a lofty recluse. If even one of these three is lacking, he still belongs among calculating recluses. Calculating reclusion is not outstanding virtue; foolish reclusion does not accord with human feelings; stone-like reclusion does not accord with the Way; lofty reclusion is not sagehood. Those six men were all mistaken. Anyone who admires their reputations and follows them merely compounds error by treading in the footsteps of error.
Alas! The duty between ruler and minister pervades heaven and earth: trying to escape it is like trying to escape the rain—there is nowhere one can go where it does not apply. To tread upon the ruler’s soil yet seek to keep oneself unsullied is wrong. To appropriate a reputation while pretending to cast reputation aside is wrong. To say that reclusion alone is lofty is wrong. To say that entering service alone is base is wrong. To say that no one in the world understands me is doubly wrong. A person’s body contains his mind, and his mind contains his understanding: each person has one mind, and each mind one understanding. Thus one person cannot withstand the scrutiny of ten people, yet those scrutinizing him number more than ten; one mind cannot withstand the doubts of ten minds, yet those doubting him number more than ten. As for those six men, hundreds and thousands of generations ago…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
人也千百世之下且猶揭肺腑而定臧否
也矧當其時乎語曰楚璧稱璞腐鼠亦稱
璞月旦稱朔車輈亦稱朔名實相溷往往
有之然而卒有能辨之者甚矣哉君子之
出處不可不審也
alt_text:

璞月旦稱朔車軥亦稱朔名實相溷往往

出處不可不審也
punctuated: 人也，千百世之下，且猶揭肺腑而定臧否也，矧當其時乎？語曰：「楚璧稱璞，腐鼠亦稱璞；月旦稱朔，車輈亦稱朔。」名實相溷，往往有之，然而卒有能辨之者。甚矣哉，君子之出處不可不審也！
translation_en: …were men of ages past; even hundreds and thousands of generations later, their innermost thoughts are still laid bare and judgments made of their merits and faults. How much more so in their own time! As the saying goes: “Jade from Chu is called pu; a rotten rat is also called pu. The first day of the month is called shuo; a carriage shaft is also called shuo.” Confusion between names and realities often occurs, yet in the end there are those who can distinguish them. How imperative it is that a gentleman carefully consider whether to enter public service or withdraw!

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the yimao year, the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing [1555], Shuntian Prefecture held its Provincial Examination for scholars. The prefectural officials requested the appointment of examiners to assess the writings, and His Majesty commanded your servants Weizhen and Wei to go and preside over it. Reverently fulfilling our charge, we compiled a record of the scholars and their writings to present to the throne. Your servant Wei is obliged by his office to offer some words.

Your servant humbly considers that, when worthy and talented men are born, the endowment and nurture of their natural dispositions and capacities depend on local conditions. Yet their growth and flourishing, their distinction and accomplishments, and their useful service to the world are truly nurtured by His Majesty’s transforming influence. As for being stirred by encouragement and moved to aspiration, and mutually tempering and honing themselves to establish meritorious achievements and moral integrity, these depend on the aspirations of the worthy and talented themselves. Yet local conditions differ in their constitution [?], and those bounded by them …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有純駁至化機則融之矣道
化普物所入有淺深至嚮往
則壹之矣臣嘗覽古傳記中
稱燕趙幽冀之間其地深厚
踔遠代產竒俊沈毅𢠢慨喜
功名之士乃今被
命掄材獲觀人士之所為文則見
===
其陳說性命究極理道其詞
若渾金璞玉光彩不炫而徐
察其精英所溢穎曄敷彪著
莫可掩遏至論述治體條列
時宜語及兵機民隱之失得
則又憤然怫愪忠義奕宣似
欲以身嬰之而利害所勿恤

若渾金璞玉光彩不炫而徐
察其精英所潘類皞數處著
莫可掩遏至論述治體條列
時宜語及兵機民隱之失得
則又憤然怫愲忠義奕宣似
欲以身嬰之而利害所勿恤
punctuated: 有純駁，至化機則融之矣。道化普，物所入有淺深，至嚮往則壹之矣。臣嘗覽古傳記，中稱燕趙幽冀之間，其地深厚踔遠，代產竒俊沈毅𢠢慨喜功名之士。乃今被命掄材，獲觀人士之所為文，則見其陳說性命，究極理道，其詞若渾金璞玉，光彩不炫，而徐察其精英所溢，穎曄敷彪著，莫可掩遏。至論述治體，條列時宜，語及兵機民隱之失得，則又憤然怫愪，忠義奕宣，似欲以身嬰之，而利害所勿恤。
translation_en: …there are differences in purity and admixture; yet the workings of moral transformation reconcile them. The transforming influence of the Way extends everywhere, though beings receive it in differing depths; their aspirations, however, bring them into unity. Your servant has read ancient accounts describing the region of Yan, Zhao, You, and Ji as a land of depth and solidity, vast in extent, which in every generation produces men of exceptional talent, steadfast resolve, and impassioned spirit [?], eager for achievement and renown. Now, having received the command to select worthy talent, I have been able to examine the writings of its scholars. I find that, in their exposition of human nature and destiny, they probe the principles of the Way to their utmost depths. Their language resembles unrefined gold and uncut jade: its brilliance does not dazzle, but upon closer inspection its overflowing essence shines forth in conspicuous splendor [?], impossible to conceal or restrain. When they discuss the principles of government and set out measures suited to present circumstances, addressing successes and failures in military strategy and in relieving the people's hidden sufferings, they become indignant and deeply agitated. Their loyalty and righteousness shine forth, as though they wished to commit themselves personally to these affairs, heedless of advantage or harm…

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
焉臣閔既作而嘆曰傳記中
所稱其信然哉是眞竒俊沈
毅忱慨喜功名之士也士負
如此材固屹然
社稷之隷乃今濟濟焉生
聖人之朝則地産之良視篚錫珍
貢厥輕重較然章著矣不足
===

幽冀之地爲
畿服士生於其間諸所漸浸稟
仰迥殊方内乃玆瓌偉卓蹏
豈地宜獨使然哉恭惟
皇上握符御曆緯武經文三十四

焉。臣閔既作而嘆曰：「傳記中所稱，其信然哉！是眞竒俊沈毅、忱慨喜功名之士也。士負如此材，固屹然社稷之隷。乃今濟濟焉，生聖人之朝，則地産之良，視篚錫珍貢，厥輕重較然章著矣。不足以需明時之用耶？」
臣又思之：今燕趙幽冀之地爲畿服，士生於其間，諸所漸浸稟仰，迥殊方内。乃玆瓌偉卓蹏，豈地宜獨使然哉？恭惟皇上握符御曆，緯武經文，三十四
translation_en:
…Your servant Min then rose and exclaimed: “Can what the transmitted records describe indeed be true! These truly are men of extraordinary talent, deep resolve, sincerity and ardor, who delight in achievement and renown. Scholars endowed with such talents assuredly stand firm as servants of the altars of soil and grain. Now they flourish in great numbers, born under the reign of a sage. The worth of these fine men produced by this land, compared with precious tribute presented in baskets, is plainly manifest in their relative importance. Are they not sufficient to meet the needs of this enlightened age?”
Your servant further reflected: the lands of Yan, Zhao, You, and Ji now constitute the capital region. For scholars born here, the influences that permeate their lives and the examples they receive and look up to differ markedly from those elsewhere within the realm. Can their magnificent and outstanding qualities [?] be due solely to the character of the land? Reverently considering that Your Majesty has grasped the sovereign tally and governed the succession of time, weaving military prowess as the weft and civil cultivation as the warp, for thirty-four…

轂下章縫士𠩄衣被尤渥乎夫
仁義所濡沃禮樂所淑陶固
有股肱輔弼之彥忠信行道
以翊賛
帝謨若
神武威靈所變化則必有忠勇不
二心之臣出膺封疆之寄爲
punctuated: 載以来，德備君師，道隆述作。化機所運，霆舉飈發，海宇從欲於變，赩赩乎懿鑠百王遠矣！士之業鉛槧、游黌校者，即疏逖阻深，猶闓澤神化，得耀乎光明，矧轂下章縫士，厥衣被尤渥乎！夫仁義所濡沃，禮樂所淑陶，固有股肱輔弼之彥，忠信行道，以翊賛帝謨。若神武威靈所變化，則必有忠勇不二心之臣，出膺封疆之寄焉。
translation_en: …years since then, Your Majesty’s virtue has fulfilled the roles of ruler and teacher, and your Way has exalted both the transmission of inherited teachings and the creation of new institutions. Wherever the workings of your transforming influence reach, they move like thunder and tempest; all within the seas willingly undergo transformation. How resplendently your excellence surpasses that of the hundred kings of old! Scholars who devote themselves to writing and study in the schools, even in remote places cut off by formidable barriers, are still enlightened and enriched by your divine transforming influence and enabled to shine in its radiance. How much more richly, then, are the scholars in their scholarly caps beneath the imperial carriage—in the capital—clothed in your bounty! Nurtured by benevolence and righteousness, and cultivated through ritual and music, there will assuredly be outstanding men to serve as your limbs and supporting counselors, practicing the Way with loyalty and trustworthiness to assist your imperial plans. As for those transformed by your divine martial prowess and awe-inspiring power, there will certainly be loyal and courageous servants of undivided allegiance who come forward to assume responsibility for the frontiers.

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
國家樹蕃屏平險阻以靖不恭
爾多士既
培毓有年而操挾軼異茲非他
日所宅才地耶
聖天子受命穆清德浸裨海率俾
之化罔有内外顧屬者蕞夷
匪茹上厪
===
宸慮寤寐疇咨思得奇俊沈毅之
賢委以綏攘大計爾多士抱
超逸之具遘會
熈明繼自今登儁將奉
大對擢
制科服休采於周行寧不思扶義
俶儻不令巳失時立功名於

punctuated:
國家樹蕃屏，平險阻，以靖不恭。爾多士既培毓有年，而操挾軼異，茲非他日所宅才地耶？
聖天子受命穆清，德浸裨海，率俾之化，罔有内外。顧屬者蕞夷匪茹，上厪宸慮，寤寐疇咨，思得奇俊沈毅之賢，委以綏攘大計。爾多士抱超逸之具，遘會熈明，繼自今登儁，將奉大對，擢制科，服休采於周行，寧不思扶義俶儻，不令巳失時，立功名於
translation_en:
The state establishes protective bulwarks and overcomes dangers and obstacles to pacify the insubordinate. You assembled scholars have been nurtured for many years, and the abilities you possess are extraordinary. Is this not the sphere in which your talents will one day find their place?
The sagely Son of Heaven has received Heaven’s mandate and dwells in august serenity. His virtue suffuses even the surrounding seas, bringing all under its transforming influence, without distinction between inner and outer realms. Yet recently petty barbarians have refused submission [?], troubling His Majesty’s mind. Waking and sleeping, he seeks counsel, hoping to find men of outstanding talent, profound resolve, and steadfastness, to entrust with the great plans for pacification and repelling aggression. You assembled scholars possess exceptional abilities and have encountered an age of flourishing and enlightened rule. Henceforth, as you rise among the outstanding men selected, you will present your answers at the Palace Examination, gain advancement through imperially prescribed examinations, and perform distinguished service in the ranks of officials. Surely you must think of upholding righteousness with bold and untrammeled spirit, not letting the opportunity slip away, and establishing achievement and renown throughout …

title: 嘉靖三十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天下哉且夫睎炎景者不隱
迹赴洪響者必急節躡
昌隆之運者不後事而昧幾奮
義建功達人所鶩以不朽也
藉令多士隤生平所許可持
空文調當世用徒欲希取一
時光寵堇堇焉私便其圖則
===
多士將躬耻之而主司亦有
滋懼矣故臣於其始進也稽
地宜本
聖化勵其嚮往之志以相成云
翰林院侍講袁煒謹序

===

滋懼矣故臣於其始進也稽
地宜本
聖化勵其嚮往之志以相成云
翰林院侍講袁煒謹序
punctuated:
天下哉？且夫睎炎景者不隱迹，赴洪響者必急節，躡昌隆之運者不後事而昧幾。奮義建功，達人所鶩以不朽也。藉令多士隤生平所許可，持空文調當世用，徒欲希取一時光寵，堇堇焉私便其圖，則多士將躬耻之，而主司亦有滋懼矣。故臣於其始進也，稽地宜，本聖化，勵其嚮往之志，以相成云。
翰林院侍講袁煒謹序。
translation_en:
…throughout the realm? Moreover, those who aspire to the blazing light do not hide their tracks; those who hasten toward a mighty sound must quicken their pace. Those who advance with an age of flourishing prosperity do not lag behind events and remain blind to opportunities. To rise in righteousness and establish achievements—this is what men of understanding pursue to attain immortality.
Suppose you scholars were to abandon what you had pledged yourselves to throughout your lives [?], offering empty literary compositions to meet the practical needs of the age, seeking merely to obtain a moment’s glory and favor, and narrowly pursuing your own advantage. Then you yourselves would feel ashamed, and the presiding examiners would have still greater cause for apprehension. Thus, as you begin your advancement, I, your servant, have considered what befits this region, taken the sage sovereign’s transforming influence as my foundation, and encouraged your aspirations, thereby helping you bring them to fulfillment.
Preface respectfully written by Yuan Wei, Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
